TOKYO, FEBe 1 (AP)-RED CHINA TODAY LABELLED NEW ZEALAND'S PROPOSAL 
FOR A CEASE-FIRE IN THE FORMOSA STRAIT “ONLY ONE OF THE STEPS IN 


THE UNITED STATES' CEASE-FIRE TRICK" AND DECLARED IT “CONTRAVENES 
THE CHARTER OF THE UNITED NATIONS.” : 

THE COMMUNISTS ALSO REITERATED THEIR THREAT TO LIBERATE FORMOSA 
AND THE PESCADORES AND SAID THEY WOULD “NOT TOLERATE ANY FOREIGN 
INTERVENTION” IN THEIR “JUST STRUGGLE." 

QUOTING FROM THE OFFICIAL NEWSPAPER, PEIPING PEOPLES’ DAILY, 


PEIPING RADIO DECLARED? 
®WHILE THREATENING WAR IN THE TAIWAN (FORMOSA) AREA, THE UNITED 

STATES IS ALSO ENGINEERING A SO-CALLED CEASE-FIRE THROUGH THE 

UNITED NATIONS. THEIR PRETEXT IS THAT THE NAVAL AND AIR FORCES 

WHICH THE UNITED STATES HAS AMASSED IN THE TAIWAN STRAIT ARE 

INTENDED TO HELP IN THE WITHDRAWAL OF THE TROOPS OF THE TRAITOR 

SHIANG KAI-SHEK FROM THE TACHEN ISLANDS. THIS PRETEXT ITSELF IS 

DIRECT ARMED INTERVENTION IN CHINA'S INTERNAL AFFAIRS." 

THE ONLY SOLUTION, PEIPING SAID, LIES WITH THE RUSSIAN DEMAND FOR 
THE IMMEDIATE WITHDRAWAL OF U.S. ARMED FORCES FROM THE FORMOSA AREA 
AND THE SURRENDER OF THE COASTAL ISLANDS TO THE COMMUNISTS. 

"THE PROPOAL PUT FORTH BY THE SOVIET DEGATE (IN THE UNITED 
NATIONS) IS CONSISTENT WITH THE COMMON ASPIRATIONS OF ALL WHO REALLY 
WAVE THE INTERESTS OF PEACE AT HEART,® PEIPING SAID. “IF THE SECURITY 
COUNCIL REALLY WANTS TO TAKE UP ITS SOLEMN DUTY OF PRESERVING PEACE, 
IT SHOULD CONSIDER THE PROPOSAL WITH THE LEAST POSSIBLE DELAY."

NATIONS. THE MATTERS IT RAISES ARE ENTIRELY INTERNAL AFFAIRS OF | 
CHINA, WHICH THE UNITED NATIONS HAS NO RIGHT WHATEVER TO DISCUSS.

* NEW be FI FEBei (AP)-IN THE FIRST TEST OF A LAW DESIGNED TO GET 


WERS FROM WITNESSES WHO INVOKE THE FIFTH AMENDMENT, A FEDERAL 
AUDGE TODAY GRANTED IMMUNITY TO WILLIAM LUDWIG ULLMAN--CITED 
2EPEATEDLY AS A SUSPECTED SOVIET SPY RING MEMBER. 

ULLMAN, 47, REFUSED TWO MONTHS AGO TO ANSWER QUESTIONS OF A GRAND 
JURY INVESTIGATING ESPIONAGE AND SUBVERSION. 

IN SEVERAL EARLIER APPEARANCES BEFORE CONGRESSIONAL INVESTIGATING 
SOMMITTEES, HE TOOK THE SAME STAND, CLAIMING THE PRIVILEGE OF THE 
FIFTH AMENDMENT TO THE CONSTITUTION. 

UNDER A LAW PASSED AT THE LAST SESSION OF CONGRESS, FEDERAL JUDGE 
EDWARD WEINFELD GRANTED IMMUNITY TO ULLMAN. THIS MEANS HE CANNOT 
LATER BE PROSECUTED FOR FEDERAL OFFENSES ON THE BASIS OF TESTIMONY 
HE GIVES TO THE AUTHORIZED BODY. 

THE FIFTH AMENDMENT PROVIDES THAT A WITNESS CANNOT BE COMPELLED 
TO INCRIMINATE HIMSELF. THE IMMUNITY LAW IS DESIGNED TO CUT THE 
SROUNDS FROM UNDER THIS REFUSAL--IF HE IS IMMUNE TO PROSECUTION 
BECAUSE OF HIS TESTIMONY, HE CANNOT CLAIM THAT HE WOULD BE 


INCRIMINATED. 
UsSe ATTORNEY J.sEDWARD LUMBARD SAID AS SOON AS WEINFELD SIGNS THE 
GRAND JURY TO QUESTION ULLMAN, 


NECESSARY art 71 HE WILL RECONVENE A 
RNEYS OPPOSED THE IMMUNITY APPLICATION ON THE GROUNDS 


ULLMAN'S ATT 
THAT THE LAW IS UNCONSTITUTIONAL AND VIOLATES HIS RIGHTS UNDER THE

BALTIMORE, FEB. 1 (AP)-SEN. DOUGLAB® (D-ILL) TONIGHT ATTRIBUTED 
WHAT HE CALLED A GROWING UNWILLINGNESS TO FIGHT COMMUNISM TO A REPURLI- 
CAN EMPHASIS ON "PEACE AT ANY PRICE.® 

IN A SPEECH TO ABOUT 500 WHO PAID $5 EACH TO ATTEND THE 7TH ANNUAL 
ROOSEVELT DAY DINNER SPONSORED BY THE AMERICANS FOR DEMOCRATIC ACTION, 
DOUGLAS SAID IT WAS HIS OPINION THAT “TYRANNY IS WORSE THAN WAR." 

"IF WE SAY THAT WE WILL NOT FIGHT, THE COMMUNISTS WILL TAKE FULL 
ADVANTAGE OF THIS AND PUSH FROM VICTORY To VICTORY," HE ADDED. 

SWITCHING TO LAST FALL'S CONGRESSIONAL CAMPAIGNS, DOUGLAS SAID THE 
REPUBLICANS INITIATED “TOTAL WAR IN POLITICS* AND DEFINED THIS AS WAR 
WHICH AIMS NOT ONLY AT DEFEATING THE ENEMY BUT ALSO ATTEMPTS TO SEF TO 
IT THAT THE ENEMY CAN NOT SURVIVE AFTER THE WAR IS OVER. 

"SUCH TACTICS." HE SAID, “THREATEN THE FOUNDATION OF AMERICAN 
DEMOCRACY BY MISLEADING THE PEOPLE AND INFLAMMING THEIR PASSIONS TO 
HATRED. 

IN ADDITION THEY THREATEN THE NATIONAL UNITY, DOUGLAS SAID. 

HE ADDED THAT ALTHOUGH THE DEMOCRATS WANT TO’ COOPERATE WITH THE 
REPUBLICAN ADMINISTRATION, HE DOES NOT BELIEVE SUCH COOPERATION FULLY 
POSSIBLE UNTIL THE REPUBLICANS APOLOGIZE FOR THEIR “SMEAR TACTICS" IN 
THE LAST CONGRESSIONAL CAMPAIGN. 

SEN. DOUGLAS EXHIBITED A SERIES OF POSTERS WHICH HE SAID WERE 
GATHERED FROM ALL PARTS OF THE COUNTRY AND WHICH HE INFERRED HAD THE 
APPROVAL OF THE REPUBLICAN NATIONAL COMMITTEF. 

IN THE POSTERS, DOUGLAS SAID, THE REPUBLICANS “ATTEMPTED TO PIN THE 
LABEL OF WAR PARTY ON THE DEMOCRATS AND TO BLAME THEM FOR CASUALTIES 
IN THE KOREAN WAR.” 

HE ESTIMATED THE “REPUBLICAN SMEAR CAMPAIGN® COST THE DEMOCRATS 
THREE SEATS IN THE SENATE AND FROM 20 TO 25 HOUSE SEATS AS WELL AS 
300,000 VOTES IN ILLINOIS. 

tHE NATURAL REACTION TO THIS TYPE CAMPAIGN WAS TO RETALIATE, HE 
ADDED. BUT THE DEMOCRATS SUCCESSFUL RESISTED THIS TEMPTATION AND 
CONDUCTED THEIR CAMPAIGN ON A HIGH LEVEL THROUGHOUT, DOUGLAS SAID.

TAIPEH, FORMOSA, FEB. 2 (AP)-THE 538 REFUGEES WHO REACHED FORMOSA 
TODAY FROM THE TACHEN ISLANDS HAD A HARROWING 200 MILE JOURNEY, 

SMALL JUNKS CARRIED THEM UNDER COVER OF DARKNESSS FROM THE TACHENS 
TO NANKISHAN, A NATIONALIST ISLAND 80 MILES SOUTH. 

THEY EMBARKED THERE ON A 3,000-TON TRANSPORT THAT WAS TO CARRY 
THEM TO FORMOSA AND SAFETY--AND ALMOST IMMEDIATELY FOUND THEMSELVES 
THREATENED BY FOUR COMMUNIST GUNBOATS. 

NATIONALIST WARSHIPS ESCORTING THE TRANSPORT RACED TO MEET THE 
CHALLENGE AND THE REDS BEAT A HASTY RETREAT. 

_ DURING THE TRIP A BABY WAS BORN TO MRS. CHANG YU-HUA. 
WAS KILLED IN THE RECENT RED INVASION OF YIKIANGSHAN. 

THERE ARE STILL SOME 15,000 CIVILIANS ONTHE TACHENS.

LON » 2 (AP)-INDIA'S JAWAHARLAL NEHRU APPEALED TODA 
A STANDSTILL AGREEMENT ON HYDROGEN-BOMB EXPLOSIONS. HE ADDRESSED™ 
FELLOW PRIME MINISTERS OF THE BRITISH COMMONWEALTH CONFERRING IN 
SECRECY ON NEW MOVES TO HEAD OFF ANY ATOMIC WAR. 

BRITAIN'S WINSTON CHURCHILL LAUNCHED THE TALKS. THE DISCUSSION 
WAS REPORTED TO HAVE INCLUDED THE QUESTION OF HOW THE GLOBE- 
ENCIRCLING COMMONWEALTH, WHICH HAS A FOURTH OF THE WORLD'S 
POPULATION, COULD CARRY ON IN CASE BRITAIN HERSELF WAS KNOCKED OUT 
BY H- IBS e 

INFORMANTS SAID NEHRU, LEADER OF A NEUTRALIST ASIAN BLOC, URGED 
THE PRIME MINISTERS OF THE EIGHT OTHER COMMONWEALTH NATIONS TO 
SUPPORT A PROPOSAL CALLING FOR A HALT IN H-BOMB TESTS WHICH WOULD 
BE PLACED BEFORE THE UNITED NATIONS DISARMAMENT SUBCOMMITTEE. THE 
COMMITTEE MEETS HERE LATER THIS MONTH. 

THE UNITED STATES HAS EXPLODED AN H=BOMB. RUSSIA CLAIMS THE 
UNITED STATES HAS NO MONOPOLY ON THE BOMB. BRITAIN IS BELIEVED 
TO BE DEVELOPING AN H-BOMB, BUT THERE HAS BEEN NO OFFICIAL 
CONFIRMATION. 

EXPERTS HERE BELIEVE FIVE H-BOMBS WOULD BE ENOUGH TO DISORGANIZE 
RESISTANCE IN BRITAIN AND 10 WOULD BLOT OUT VIRTUALLY ALL MAIN 
CENTERS OF INDUSTRY, WHERE HALF OF THE POPULATION OF 50 MILLION 
LIVES. 

SUCH AN ATTACK WOULD KNOCK OUT THE NERVE CENTER OF COMMONWEALTH 
COMMUNICATIONS AND NECESSITATE EMERGENCY CHANGES IN THE 
COMMONWEALTH'S DEFENSE AND ECONOMY. 

THE PRIME MINISTERS ALSO CONSIDERED HOW ATOMIC POWER CAN BE PUT 
TO WORK IN INDUSTRY THROUGHOUT THE COMMONWEALTH.

LONDON, FEBe 2 (AP)-BRITAIN IS REVIEWING HER POLICYY OF EXTENDING 
DIPLOMATIC IMMUNITY TO ALL MEMBERS OF THE MISSIONS OF IRON CURTAIN 
COUNTRIES, THE HOUSE OF. LORDS WAS TOLD TODAY. 

LORD READING MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOREIGN AFFAIRS,. SAID SOVIET AND 
OTHER IRON CURTAIN COUNTRIES ARE EXTENDING PERSONAL IMMUNITY ONLY TO 
HEADS OF FOREIGN DIPLOMATIC MISSIONS AND NOT TO SUBORDINATE OR 
NON-DIPLOMATIC MISSION MEMBERS. SUCH IMMUNITY BY INTERNATIONAL CUSTOM 
PROTECTS DIPLOMATIC STAFFS FROM ARREST OR MOLESTATION. es ree 

THE REVIEW IS BEING UNDERTAKEN WITH A VIEW TO APPLYING THE 19559

MOSCOW, FEB. 2 (AP)-THE SOVIET PRESS. IN INUING CAMPAIGN TO 
BLOCK RATIFICATION OF THE PARIS AGREEMENTS FOR REAWMING WEST GERMANY, 
IS SAYING AN ATOMIC WAR WOULDWIT DENSELY POPULATED WEST EUROPE FIRST 
AND HARDEST, AND ALSO SERIOUSLY WOUND THE UNITED STATES 
__ THE LATEST TO ISSUE SUCH A WARNING IS MAJ. GEN. NeTALENSKYy o 9 = 
WRITING IN THE MAGAZINE INTERNATIONAL LIFE. iy Id 

BUT, WHILE CLAIMING THAT THE UNITED STATES WILL “SUFFER ALSO 
IN AN ATOMIC WAR, TALENSKY DOESN'T HIDE THE FACT THAT THE SOVIET UNION 
WOULD SUFFER IN ADDITION TO A "GREAT PART OF THE GLOBE." 

THIS ADMISSION THAT THE SOVIET UNION WOULD BE HIT ALONG WITH THE 
REST OF THE WORLD EMPHASIZES WHAT PREMIER GEORGE MALENKOV SAID 
IN A SPEECH IN MOSCOW LAST MARCH DURING AN ELECTION CAMPAIGN FOR THE 
SUPREME SOVIET. MALENKOV ACCUSED "WESTERN IMPERIALISTS" OF "PREPARING 
A FRESH WORLD CARNAGE,” AND ADDED THAT A NEW WAR “WITH MODERN WEAPONS 
WOULD MEAN THE RUIN OF WORLD CIVILIZATION." 

CONSEQUENTLY FOR NEARLY A YEAR, RED STAR AND OTHER PAPERS HAVE BEEN 
PUBLISHING ARTICLES ADVISING CIVILIANS AND THE MILITARY ON PRECAUTIONS 
TO TAKE IN THE EVENT OF ATOMIC WAR. 


TALENSKY BASED HIS DISCUSSION OF ATOMIC WEAPONS ON REPORTS THAT THE 


NORTH ATLANTIC TREATY COUNCIL AND AMERICAN STRATEGISTS BANK MORE ON THE 


NEWEST WEAPONS THAN ON MASSED ARMED FORCESe HE DISPUTED CLAIMS THAT 
ATOMIC GUNS CAN EASILY BE USED BY FIELD ARMIES AND ASSERTED THAT 
ATOMIC WARFARE WILL SPREAD THE ZONES OF FIGHTING. 


A THIRD WORLD WAR, HE SAID, “WILL INEVITABLY EXTEND THE SPHERE OF 
MILITARY ACTION AND COVER A LARGE PART OF THE GLOBE, INCLUDING THE 
TERRITORY OF THE UNITED STATES."

FORMOSA INTERPRETIVE (230) 
BY FRED HAMPSON 

TAIPEH, FORMOSA, FEB. 3 (AP)-LONDON REPORTS THAT RED CHINA MIGHT 
AGREE TO AN UNWRITTEN CEASEFIRE IN THE TROUBLED FORMOSA AREA IN 
EXCHANSE FOR THE CHINESE NATIONALIST ISLANDS MATSU, QUEMOY AND THE 
TACHENS PRODUCED ANGRY REACTION HERE TODAY. 

SAID ONE NATIONALIST OFFICER: 

"WE START BY TALKING ABOUT THE EVACUATION OF THE TACHENS IN THE 
INTEREST OF PEACE AND NOW WE ARE TALKING ABOUT GIVING UP EVERY 
OUTLYING ISLAND.® 

CHIANG KAI-SHEK'S PEOPLE FEAR THE CRISIS, PRECIPITATED BY 
COMMUNIST SEIZURE OF TINY YIKIANGSHAN, WILL WIND UP IN WHAT THEY 
CONSIDER THE OLD AND DISCOURAGING PATTERN OF MORE CONCESSIONS TO 
THE REDS. 

IT WAS ALSO FELT HERE THAT DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN THE NATIONALISTS 
AND THE UNITED STATES IS PLAYING INTO THE HANDS OF THOSE WHO ARE 
WILLING TO GIVE THE MAXIMUM TO COMMUNIST CHINA. 

UNTIL A FEW DAYS AGO THERE WERE INDICATIONS THAT IF CHIANG AGREED 
TO EVACUATE THE EXPOSED AND THREATENED TACHENS, THE UNITED STATES 
WOULD AGREE TO HELP HIM DEFEND MATSU AND QUEMOY. , 

BUT WASHINGTON REPORTS, AT LEAST AS INTERPRETED HERE, NOW MAKE) IT 
APPEAR THAT AGREEMENT IS OUT--AT LEAST IN SPECIFIC FORM. ~4 

WHAT WILL HAPPEN IF THE WESTERN POWERS TRY TO BUY AN AGREEMENT, 
WITH PEIPING AT THE COST OF THE NATIONALISTS" OUTER ISLANDS? 

SOME OF CHIANG'S HOTHEADS SAYS THE NATIONALISTS WILL HAVE NO 
PART OF SUCH A DEAL, AND WILL STAY ON THE ISLANDS AND FIGHT.

ATOMS~FOR-PEACE 
BY WILLIAN N. OATIS 
UNITED NATIONS, NeYe, FEB. 3-(AP)-AN AMERICAN AND AN INDIAN WILL 
BE TOP MEN AT THE FIRST WORLD SCIENTIFIC CONFERENCE ON ATOMS-FOR-PEACE 
IN GENEVA NEXT AUGUST. THE U.sN.-SPONSORED PARLEY WILL DISCLOSE 
SCIENTISTS’ ESTIMATES OF THE PROSPECTS FOR NUCLEAR POWER IN THE 
NEXT 25 TO 50 YEARS. 
THE AMERICAN, WALTER GORDON WHITMAN, 59, OF CONCORD, MASS», WILL BE 
THE SECRETARY GENERAL, IN CHARGE OF ARRANGEMENTS. HE IS A PIONEER 
RESEARCHER IN AIRCRAFT PROPULSION FOR THE U.S. ATOMIC ENERGY 
COMMISSION, MEMBER OF THE AEC’S GENERAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE AND 
DIRECTOR OF THE DEFENSE DEPARTMENT'S RESEARCH BOARD. 
HOMI JEHANGIR BHABHA, 45, OF BOMBAY, CHAIRMAN OF INDIA'S ATOMIC 
ENERGY COMMISSION AND SECRETARY OF ITS DEPARTMENT OF ATOMIC ENERGY, 
WILL BE CONFERENCE PRESIDENT, ENPOWERED TO RULE OUT POLITICAL 


DISCUSSION. 
UeNe SECRETARY GENERAL DAG HAMMARSKJOLD ANNOUNCED THEIR APPOINT- 


.MENTS LAST NIGHT IN LETTERS INVITING 84 COUNTRIES--10 OF THEM COMMUNIST 


=-TO SEND FIVE OFFICIAL DELEGATES EACH TO THE CONGRESS. 
| HE ENCLOSED AN AGENDA AND RULES FOR THE "INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE 
'ON THE PEACEFUL USES OF ATOMIC ENERGY," TO START AUG. 8 IN THE OLD 

! LEAGUE OF NATIONS PALACE AND LAST 12 WORKING DAYS.» 

THE RULES, FORMULATED BY A SEVEN-NATION ADVISORY COMMITTEE OF 

, SCIENTISTS WHICH MET HERE JAN. 17-28, SPECIFY THAT THE CONFERENCE IS 
‘FOR EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION ONLY. ONE PROVISION READS: “NO 
‘PROPOSALS REQUIRING ADOPTION BY VOTING SHALL BE SUBMITTED OR 

) ENTERTAINED BY THE CONFERENCE." | 

THE COMMITTEE ALSO AGREED THAT THE CONFERENCE PROCEEDINGS WILL BE 

| PUBLISHED.

HAMMARSKJOLD ALSO SENT WITH THE INVITATIONS AN ANNOUNCEMENT THAT 
THE SOVIET UNION PLANS TO REPORT TO THE CONFERENCE ON "THE U.S.s.p.t 
FIRST ATOMIC POWER PLANT FOR INDUSTRIAL PURPOSES AND METHODS oF” &gt; 
DEVELOPING ATOMIC POWER." THE RUSSIANS SAY THEY BEGAN OPERATING such 
A PLANT, GENERATING 5,000 KILOWATTS OF ELECTRICITY, LAST SUMMER. 

JeVe DUNWORTH, BRITISH SCIENTIST ON HAMMARSKJOLB'S SEVEN-NATION 
ADVISORY COMMITTEE FOR THE CONFERENCE, SAID IN AN INTERVIEW 
HERE LAST NIGHT THAT BRITAIN WOULD PRESENT SEVERAL REPORTS ON HER 
WORK ON ATOMIC POWER. HE SAID THE BRITISH EXPECT TO HAVE A 50,009- 
KILOWATT ATOMIC GENERATOR, THEIR FIRST, IN OPERATION NEXT YEAR, 
NUCLEAR ENERGY "LOOKS VERY ATTRACTIVE,* HE EXPLAINED, BECAUSE 
BRITAIN FORESEES A BIG FUEL SHORTAGE WITHIN 20 YEARS. 

THE UNITED STATES ALREADY IS PRODUCING ELECTRICITY AT TWO SMALL 
EXPERIMENTAL PLANTS, ONE AT THE AEC'S REACTOR TESTING STATION IN 
IDAHO AND THE OTHER AT OAK RIDGE, TENN. 

THE UsNe GENERAL ASSEMBLY CALLED FOR THE CONFERENCE IN A RESOLUTION 
ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY LAST DEC. 4 AS THE OUTGROWTH OF PRESIDENT 
EISENHOWER'S "ATOMS-FOR-PEACE" SPEECH A YEAR EARLIER. 

THE RESOLUTION SAID INVITATIONS SHOULD GO TO ALL U.N. MEMBERS 
(60 NATIONS, INCLUDING SOVIET-BLOC CZECHOSLOVAKIA, POLAND, RUSSIA, 
WHITE RUSSIA AND THE UKRAINE AND INDEPENDENT-COMMUNIST YUGOSLAVIA) 
AND ALL NON-MEMBERS BELONGING TO ANY U.sNe SPECIALIZED AGENCIES (24 
NATIONS. INCLUDING COMMUNIST ALBANIA, BULGARIA, HUNGARY AND ROMANIA). 


THE 14-PAGE AGENDA ADOPTED BY THE SCIENTISTS’ COMMITTEE LISTS MORE 
THAN 100 TOPICS FOR DISCUSSION BY THE FULL CONFERENCE AND BY SIX 
SPECIAL SECTIONS. 

THE FULL PLENARY SESSIONS WILL TAKE UP SUCH MAJOR ITEMS AS: 

(1) THE WORLD'S POWER NEEDS IN 25 TO 50 YEARS AND HOW FAR ATOMIC 
ENERGY CAN BE DEVELOPED TO HELP MEET THEM, ESPECIALLY IN COUNTRIES 
NOT YET INDUSTRIALIZED; (2) HOW TO DISPOSE SAFELY OF DANGEROUS 

ATOMIC WASTES AND PROTECT PEOPLE FROM RADIOACTIVE CONTAMINATION; 

(3) HOW TO MAKE USE OF RADIOACTIVE ISOTOPES IN INDUSTRY, MEDICINE 
BIOLOGY AND AGRICULTURE; AND (4) WHAT HELP THE VARIOUS GOVERNMENTS ARF 
GIVING OTHER COUNTRIES IN SUCH FIELDS. ? 

SECTION MEETINGS WILL DEAL WITH RESEARCH AND POWER REACTORS CATOMIC 
PILES), PROCESSING OF THE ATOMIC FUELS URANIUM AND THORIUM, REACTOR 
PHYSIC$, REACTOR CHEMISTRY AND METALLURGY, BIOLOGICAL AND MEDICAL 
CONSIDERATIONS AND DETAILS OF THE USES OF RADIOACTIVE ISOTOPES. 

WHITMAN. WHO ATTENDED THE FIRST TWO MEETINGS OF THE ADVISORY 
COMMITTEE AS A U.S. REPRESENTATIVE, IS SCHEDULED TO RETURN TO U.N. 
HEADQUARTERS TUESDAY TO BEGIN FURTHER ARRANGEMENTS. FOR THE CONFERENCE.

CO. OF INDIANA. IN 1948 HE DIRECTED THE AEC'S LEXINGTON PROJECT, WHICH 
SHOWED THE FEASIBILITY OF ATOM-POWERED AIRPLANES.

AND AT CAMBRIDGE. A THEORETICAL PHYSICIST, HE NOW DIRECTS THE TATA 
INSTITUTE OF FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH IN BOMBAY

AVOIDING A_MAJOR CLASH OFF THE CHINA COAST NOW THAT RED CHINA HAS

KWANGMING DAILY AND PEIPING NEWSPAPERS CONCERNING FORMOSA, THE

ATTACKED THE ESCORTING JET FIGHTERS FLYING TOP COVER." 

THE SABRES, WHICH RAN UP A 12-1 EDGE OVER MIGS IN THE KOREAN WAR 
WERE FROM THE FOURTH FIGHTER-INTERCEPTOR WING TRANSFERRED FROM JAPAN 
_TO FORWARD BASES IN KOREA DURING THE PRESENT FORMOSA CRISIS. 


(IN WASHINGTON, SPOKESMEN FOR THE DEFENSE AND STATE DEPARTMENTS 
SAID THEY HAD NO INFORMATION ON THE CLASH.) 

THE INCIDENT WAS SIMILAR TO ONE SLIGHTLY OVER A YEAR AGO WHEN 
SABRES ESCORTING ANOTHER RB4&amp;S OVER THE YELLOW SEA SHOT DOWN ONE MIG 
AFTER A FLIGHT OF MIGS ATTACKED. 

THE RB4S IS A FAST MEDIUM JET BOMBER CONVERTED INTO A RECON- 
NAISSANCE PLANE LOADED WITH CAMERAS AND RADAR SEARCH EQUIPMENT. 

THE PLANES HAVE BEEN FLYING UP THE COASTS OF KOREA OUTSIDE THE 
THREE MILE LIMIT FOR MORE THAN TWO YEARS. THEY OR SIMILAR AIRCRAFT, 
BEGAN SUCH PATROLS IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE KOREAN ARMISTICE IN THE 
SUMMER OF 1953 AFTER THE END OF THE WAR AGREEMENT BARRED THE ALLIES 
FROM FLYING OVER NORTH KOREA ITSELF. 

TODAY'S AIR BATTLE WAS THE FIRST AIR INCIDENT IN THE FAR EAST 
COMMAND SINCE*TWO SOVIET MIGS BASED EITHER ON THE KURILES OR THE 
HABOMAIS SHOT DOWN A SLOWER AMERICAN RB-29 OFF THE EAST COAST 
OF HOKKAIDO ON NOV. 7, 1954. ONE CREWMEN ABOARD THE RECONNAISSANCE 
BOMBER WAS KILLED IN PARACHUTING. 

THE REDS CLAIMED THE AMERICAN PLANE, WHICH WAS ON A PHOTO MAPPING 
MISSION, WAS OVER RED TERRITORY. THIS WAS DENIED VIGOROUSLY BY GEN, 
JOHN E. HULL, THE FAR EAST COMMANDER, AND BY THE AIR FORCE.

AND COMMUNIST AIRCRAFT IN THE TENSE SKY FRONTIER BETWEEN

BY FRED HAMPSON 
FORMOSA, SUNDAY, FEBe6 (AP)-THE MISSION ASSIGNED THE U.S. 

7TH FLEET OF WITHDRAWING THE NATIONALIST GARRISON FROM THE TACHENS HAS 
BEEN CALLED "A TWO-BIT TASK WITH BILLION DOLLAR RISKS." 

THE DANGER LIES IN THE RED REACTION. 

IF THE REDS OPPOSE WITH FORCE THE WITHDRAWAL OF SOME 15,000 SOLDIERS 
AND THEIR EQUIPMENT, ALONG WITH 15,000 CIVILIANS, IT COULD MEAN 
WARe IT COULD BE A LOCALIZED AIR-SEA WARe IT COULD BE FULL-SCALE 
UeSe-CHINA WAR. IT COULD CONCEIVABLY GROW INTO GLOBAL ATOMIC WAR. 

WHATEVER HAPPENS, THE REDS CAN BE COUNTED ON TO MAKE TERRIFIC PRPA- 
GANDA CLAIMS. THEIR LINE WILL BE THAT THEIR CAPTURE OF THE TINY ISLANI 
OF YIKIANGSHAN EIGHT MILES NORTH OF THE TACHENS CHASED OUT THE 
NATIONALISTS. 

THE REDS STILL ARE TRUMPETING THEIR INTENTION OF "LIBERATING" 
FORMOSA. THE IMPENDING TACHEN WITHDRAWAL COULD EASILY BE CONSTRUED 
BY THE REDS AS A VICTORIOUS CHAPTER TO THIS END. 

THERE IS STILL ROOM TO SQUEEZE PAST THIS IMPASSE WITHOUT WAR, 
ALTHOUGH THE UNITED STATES DID NOT SPELL OUT A PROMISE TO DEFEND

PY TONDON, FEB. 5 (AP)-BRITISH DIPLOMATIC INFORMANTS HINTED STRONGLY 
TONIGHT RUSSIA HAS JOINED WITH BRITAIN AND INDIA IN SECRET EFFORTS TO 
GET AN “UNWRITTEN® CEASE-FIRE IN THE FORMOSA STRAIT. 

THE SOVIETS, ADMITTEDLY FEARFUL OF A MAJOR WAR» WERE UNDERSTOOD TO 
BE TRYING TO STAY RED CHINA'S TRIGGERS WHILE AT THE SAME TIME 
MANEUVERING TO GET THEM CONCESSIONS IN THE FORMOSA DISPUTE. 

RUSSIA, BRITAIN_AND INDIA HAVE EXCHANGED VIEWS REPEATEDLY ABOUT 
FORMOSA BOTH BEFORE AND AFTER PEIPING TURNED DOWN THE U.N. INVITATION 
TO TALK PEACE. 

TONIGHT INFORMANTS INDICATED RUSSIA IS READY TO TRY TO RESTRAIN 
PEIPING WHILE BRITAIN AND INDIA IMPRESS UPON THE UNITED STATES THAT A 
TIGHT LEASH MUST ALSO BE RETAINED ON CHIANG KAI-SHEK. 

BRITAIN AND. INDIA -ARE. IN-AGREEMENT WITH-RUSSIA—THAT THE CHINESE 
REDS HAVE LEGAL RIGHTS TO CHIANG'S OFFSHORE ISLANDS--THE QUEMOY 
MATSU AND TACHEN GROUPS. BUT BRITAIN BELIEVES THESE ISLANDS SHOULD 
GO TO THE REDS ONLY AS PART OF A CEASE- , 

BRITAIN AND INDIA ARGUE THAT FORMOSA AND THE PESCADORES SHOULD 
REMAIN IN CHIANG'S HANDS AND THEIR ULTIMATE FUTURE BE DECIDED LATE 
AROUND A CONFERENCE TABLE.

LS OF BRITAIN TONIGHT WITH DENUNCIATIONS OF CHIANG KAI-SHEK 
AND OF ANY IDEAS OF DEFENDING HIS FORMOSA BASTION. 

THE SAME THEME WAS VOICED BY MODERATES AND BEVANITE LEFT-WINGERS. 

DRe EDITH SUMMERSKILL, PARTY CHAIRMAN, TOLD A MEETING IN SUSSEX? 

"THIS IS THE TIME FOR PLAIN SPEAKING. CHIANG KAI=SHEK SHOULD 
BE TOLD THAT THE WORKERS OF THIS COUNTRY WOULD NOT SUPPORT THE 
CLAIMS OF A DISCREDITED DICTATOR AGAINST THE WORKERS OF THE 
RECOGNIZED GOVERNMENT OF THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA. HE SHOULD 
BE GIVEN NOTICE TO QUIT FORTHWITH AND THE ISLAND NEUTRALIZED.® 

SHE CHARGED THE “BOGUS GOVERNMENT OF FORMOSA® WAS SOLELY CONCERNED 
WITH "ADMINISTERING A UNITED STATES BASE" AND SAID THE FAR EAST HOLDS 
ALL THE INGREDIENTS OF A WORLD WAR. 

LEFTIST ANEURIN BEVAN, SPEAKING TO MINEWORKERS IN YORKSHIRE SAID, 
"WE SHOULD TELL THE UNITED STATES THAT IT SHOULD NOT BE 
DECEIVED INTO SACRIFICING A SINGLE LIFE IN ORDER TO GET CHIANG 
KAI=SHEK BACK INTO CHINA.” HE ADDED, “WHAT WE SHOULD BE SAYING TO THE 
UNITED STATES AT THIS MOMENT IS THAT THE WAY TO MAKE PEACE IS TO DISARM 
CHIANG KAI-SHEK*S FORCES ON FORMOSA." 

ANTHONY GREENWOOD, A MIDDLE-OF-THE~ROAD LABORITE, SAID_ IN SURREY 
THAT AMERICA'S SECRETARY OF STATE JOHN FOSTER DULLES HAS “ABOUT AS 
MUCH SENSE AND DIPLOMACY AS A WATER BUFFALO.” GREENWOOD SAID DULLES 
BECOMES “MORE AND MORE OF A LIABILITY TO THE WESTERN POWERS” AND SHOULD

IN SAYING THAT THE SOLE REASON FOR MY ACQUIESCENCE IN THESE REDUCTIONS 
IS BASED ON A NEW POLICY OF STABILITY."

APPROXIMATELY 34 OT 35 BILLION DOLLARS A YEAR TO MAINTAIN FORCES OF THI

THE NATIONALISTS HAD BEEN SILENT FOR MORE THAN 19 HOURS AFTER 
WASHINGTON'S ANNOUNCEMENT THAT CHIANG HAD ACCEPTED U.S. HELP IN 
WITHDRAWING FROM THE TACHENS. 

THE STATEMENT, DATED SUNDAY, WAS APPROVED BY CHIANG HIMSELF BEFORE 
IT WAS PUT OUT. EVERY WORD WAS CAREFULLY CONSIDERED AND RECONSID- 
ERED, AS IS CHIANG'S HABIT. 

THE STATEMENT THAT SOLDIERS FROM THE TACHENS WILL BE REDEPLOYED 
DOES NOT IMPLY THAT THEY WILL BE MOVED IMMEDIATELY TO QUEMOY AND 
MATSU. BUT THE NATIONALISTS, TO WHOM ABANDONMENT OF THE TACHENS Is 
DISTASTEFUL, HAD TO WORD THE ANNOUNCEMENT SO AS TO SAVE AS MUCH FACE 

S POSSIBLE.

ACCORDING TO AUSTRIAN POLICE, THE SITUATION SUDDENLY ERUPTED WHEN

FACE OF ONE OF THE OTHER TWO. RUSSIANS IN UNIFORM QUICKLY ENTERED AND 
TRIED TO GRAB THE AMERICANS, BUT THEY BARRICADED THEMSELVES IN THE 
WASHROOM. AUSTRIAN POLICE ARRIVED AND FOUND EVERY DOOR GUARDED BY RUS- 
SIAN SOLDIERS. THE INTERNATIONAL POLICE PATROL CAME UP AND TOOK THE 
AMERICANS AWAY. THEY WERE TURNED OVER TO AMERICAN AUTHORITIES LATER. 

AUSTRIAN POLICE SAID THEY REGARDED THE AFFAIR AS A CLASH OF AMERICAN 
AND RUSSIAN INTELLIGENCE FORCES.

CIA--BUDGET 
BY EDWIN Be HAAKINSON 
WASHINGTON, FEBe 6 (AP)-SEN. MANSFIELD (D-MONT) SAID TODAY HE 
HAS THE PROMISED SUPPORT OF 35 OTHER SENATORS FOR HIS PROPOSAL TO SET 
UP A JOINT CONGRESSIONAL COMMITTEE "TO KEEP A CONSTANT CHECK" ON THE 


CENTRAL INTELLIGENCE AGENCY. 
"WE HAVE NO DESIRE TO PRY INTO THE NECESSARY SECRETS OF CIA," 


MANSFIELD SAID IN AN INTERVIEW, BUT HE CONTENDED THE PRESENT METHOD 
OF LETTING A FEW TOP MEMBERS OF SENATE AND HOUSE COMMITTEES CHECK THE 
SUPERSECRET AGENCY “IS A HODGEPODGE SYSTEM." 

MANSFIELD SAID THERE “HAS BEEN ALMOST NO_ CONGRESSIONAL 
INSPECTION" OF CIA SINCE IT WAS SET UP TO REPLACE THE OFFICE OF 
STRATEGIC SERVICES OF WORLD WAR II DAYS AND ONLY A FEW MEMBERS OF 
CONGRESS EVEN KNOW HOW MUCH MONEY IT SPENDS OR HOW MANY PERSONS WORK 


FOR IT. 
"I AGREE THAT AN INTELLIGENCE AGENCY MUST MAINTAIN COMPLETE 


SECRECY TO BE EFFECTIVE," HE SAID. “BUT ONCE SECRECY BECOMES SACRO- 
SANCT, IT INVITES ABUSES." 

THE MONTANA SENATOR SAID THE JOINT CIA COMMITTEE HE PROPOSES 
"WOULD OPERATE IN MUCH THE SAME MANNER AS THE PRESENT JOINT ATOMIC 


COMMITTEE OPERATES IN THAT FIELD." 
"THIS IS NOT A PROPOSAL TO INVESTIGATE CIA," HE SAID. “IT WILL 


GIVE LEADERS OF THE AGENCY A STANDING COMMITTEE TO SAFEGUARD ITS 


INTERESTS AS WELL AS THOSE OF THE CONGRESS AND THE NATION." 
HIS PROPOSAL IS, EXPECTED TO RUN INTO POWERFUL OPPOSITION OF THE 


APPROPRIATIONS AND ARMED SERVICES COMMITTEES IN BOTH THE SENATE AND 


CHAIRMAN RUSSELL (D-GA) OF THE SENATE ARMED SERVICES COMMITTEE 
DISCLOSED LAST WEEK THAT SENIOR MEMBERS OF THAT GROUP HAD BEEN 
CHECKING ON CIA FROM TIME TO TIME SINCE IT WAS SET UP BY THE @© B45 

ss 


NATIONAL SECURITY ACT OF 1947. 
SEN. BRIDGES gg FORMER CHAIRMAN OF APPROPRIATIONS AND ALSO A 
V 


TOP MEMBER OF ARMED SERVICES, CONFIRMED THIS BUT SAID HE 


BELIEVED CONGRESS SHOULD DO A BETTER JOB. 
MANSFIELD SAID THE PROPOSED JOINT COMMITTEE WOULD ASSURE CIA 


OFFICIALS “OF A FAIR HEARING WHEN CHARGES OR ACCUSATIONS ARE MADE 
AGAINST THE AGENCY."

BECKER SAID THE 7TH FLEET ARMADA COURSING OFF THE CHINA COAST 
WAS MADE UP OF 75 WARSHIPS. 

NAVY SOURCES IN WASHINGTON WERE MORE SPECIFIC. THEY LISTED 6 
FAST CARRIERS--THE MIDWAY, WASP, KEARSARGE, ESSEX, YORKTOWN AND 
PRINCETON--2 CRUISERS, 36 DESTROYERS, 5 SUBMARINES AND 15 MINE 
SWEEPERS AMONG THE COMBAT SHIPS. 

THESE DID NOT INCLUDE THE AMPHIBIOUS SHIPS OF THE U.S. AND CHINESE 
NATIONALIST NAVIES WHICH WERE ASSIGNED THE ACTUAL EVACUATION TASK. 

THE TACHENS AREA HAS BEEN MINED BY COMMUNISTS, FLEET SOURCES SAID. 
UNDERWATER DEMOLITON TEAMS AND MINE SWEEPERS WERE ASSIGNED TO PATROL 

H Ae , 

THE EVACUATIONOF THE TACHENS LOOMED AS A TOUGH CHORE, EVEN WITHOUT 
COMMUNIST OPPOSITION. 

BEACHES THERE ARE FEW AND ROCKY. TIDES RUN FROM 16 TO 18 FEET. 
SABIN SAID LOADING TIME WOULD BE CUT TO ONLY SIX HOURS DAILY. 

MUCH HEAVY EQUIPMENT MUST BE MOVED OVER THE TACHEN BEACHES. THE 
NATIONALISTS WERE DUG IN WITH HEAVY EQUIPMENT FOR A LONG STAY. 

NATIONALIST SOURCES ESTIMATED THERE WERE AT LEAST 41,688 REGULAR 
TROOPS, GUERRILLAS AND CIVILIANS ON THE TACHENS, YU SHAN AND PISHAN. 

CHIANG KAI-SHEK'S 46TH DIVISION, ABOUT 10,000 TROOPS STATIONED 
MOSTLY ON UPPER TACHEN, WILL BE BROUGHT TO FORMOSA. 

THERE WERE INDICATIONS THAT 4,000 GUERRILLAS ON THE TACHENS WOULD 
BE TAKEN TO MATSU AND QUEMOY AFTER A STOP ON NANCHISHAN ISLAND, 80 
MILES SOUTH OF THE TACHENS. SUCH A REDEPLOYMENT WOULD BE CARRIED OUT 
BY THE NATIONALIST NAVY WITH THE U.S. 7TH FLEET COVERING ONLY WITH- 
DRAWALS TO FORMOSA. 

MOST OF THE 15,000 OR MORE CIVILIANS WERE ON LOWER TACHEN. 
SOURCES SAID MOST HAD SIGNED UP TO GO, PREFERRING TO LEAVE THEIR 
HOMES RATHER THAN LIVE UNDER THE COMMUNISTS. 

CHINESE PRESS REPORTS SAID SOME HAD PLACED PLACARDS ON THEIR DOORS 
INSCRIBED: "WE ARE GONE BUT WE WILL COME BACK BEFORE LONG." 

CHINESE PRESS REPORTS SAID NANCHISHAN WOULD BE HELD AS A "NORTHERN 
SHIELD FOR FORMOSA." ABOUT 5,000 TROOPS WERE REPORTED STATIONED *

TOKYO, TUESDAY, FEB. 8 (AP)-THE ESTES, REAR ADM. LORENZO SHERWOOD 
SABIN'S FLAGSHIP FOR THE TACHENS EVACUATION, IS A 14,000-TON COMMAND 
SHIP OF THE KIND USED IN THE PACIFIC WAR LANDINGS ON’SAIPAN, IWO JIMA 

WA. 
AND TE IS A SISTER SHIP OF SUCH FAMED WORLD WAR II SHIPS AS THE MOUNT 
MCKINLEY, TETON AND ROCKY MOUNT. 

NEARLY 450 FEET LONG, SHE IS ALMOST AS BIG AS A CRUISER. 

SUCH COMMAND SHIPS ARE SPECIALLY DESIGNED FOR TWO MAIN PURPOSES -- 
CARRYING AN ADMIRAL'S HUGE TECHNICAL AND COMMAND STAFF, AND OFFERING 
THE LAST WORD IN RADAR AND RADIO COMMUNICATIONS. | 

THE ESTES IS HOME SHIP FOR AMERICAN NEWS CORRESPONDENTS WITH THE 
EVACUATION FLOTILLA, INCLUDING JIM BECKER OF THE ASSOCIATED PRESS, 
WHEN THEY ARE NOT ON THE ISLANDS THEMSELVES. - : 

NEWS STORIES OF THE EVACUATION ARE RELAYED BY RADIO FROM THE ESTES 
TO NAVY RADIO STATIONS AT YOKOSUKA, JAPAN SANGLEY POINT, THE PHILI- 
PPINES, GUAM, OR SAN FRANCISCO DIRECT, DEPENDING ON RECEPT

AHEAD OF THE FRONT LINES IN KOREA. IT TOO STANDS GUARD AGAINST A 
A SURPRISE ATTACK BY THE COMMUNISTS. 

IN A DARKENED COMPARTMENT A PENCIL LINE OF FLUORESCENCE SPEEDS 
AROUND A RADAR SCOPE, A PULSATING HAND ON A FACELESS CLOCK. 

ELECTRONIC WAVES THAT PIERCE DARKNESS, FOG, STORMS AND MILES OF 
DISTANCE SCAN THE SKIES FOR PLANES THAT €ouLD’ BE HOSTILE. 

A FEW FEET AWAY, ANOTHER SCOPE FLASHES. IT SEEKS SHIPS, ESPECIALLY 
RED CHINESE JUNK FLEETS THAT COULD BE CARRYING COMMUNIST INVADERS OR 
GUERRILLAS TO FORMOSA. 

FOUR DECKS BELOW, CONCENTRIC CIRCLES OF LIGHT BOUNCE FROM THE 
Atty OF ANOTHER SCoPE LIKE RIPPLES FROM A STONE TOSSED INTO STILL 
* ° 

FACH EXPLODING BUBBLE OF LIGHT TRIGGERS AN AUDIBLE BEEP. AN 
ECHOING PING, AN INTERRUPTING BLIP IN THE EXPANDING RINGS OF LIGHT 
COULD MEAN A STALKING SUBMARINE--OR A SCHOOL OF FISH. TRAINED EARS 
AND TRAINED EYES KNOW THE DIFFERENCE. 

OTHER SCOPES GLOW INSIDE THE DESTOYER'S ARMORED MAIN BATTERY DIRECTOR 
ATOP THE PILOT HOUSE. INTRICATELY TIED TO THE DESTOYER'S GUNS, THESE 
SCOPES CAN LOCK THE GUNS ON A TARGET THAT CANNOT BE SEEN. 

THERE IS NEVER A MOMENT WHEN THE ELECTRONIC DEVICES ARE NOT 
OPERATINGe THERE IS NEVER A MOMENT WHEN MEN WITH BINOCULARS ARE NOT

THE JOB IS EARLY DETECTION AND EARLY WARNING OF ANY RED FLEET 
MASSING THAT MIGHT PORTEND A COMMUNIST INVASION ATTEMPT OR PLANES 
THAT MIGHT BE CARRYING BOMBS TOWARD FORMOSA OR THE PESCADORES. 

MIN THE EVENT OF WAR," SAYS CMDR. Re Le COCHRANE OF SAN DIEGO, 
CAPTAIN OF THIS DESTROYER, “DECLARED OR UNDECLARED, 

WE COULD GIVE 48 TO 72 HOURS WARNING OF A SEABORNE ATTACK, AT LEAST 
4 HALF HQUR AND PROBABLY AN HOUR WARNING OF A BOMBER'S FLIGHT TOWARD 
FORMOSAe 

A MAJOR RED ATTACK, HE CONCEDES, “COULD WELL MEAN OUR ANNIHILATION” 
BECAUSE "PROBABLY WE WOULD BE THE FIRST TO BE ATTACKED BY COMMUNIST 
PLANES. 

*A FEW MILES OVER THERE IS THE CHINA MAINLAND. WE STAY OUTSIDE 
THEIR TERRITORIAL WATERS. AND OVER THERE IS FORMOSA. 

“BETWEEN 1S TECHNICALLY FREE WATER. OUR JOB IS TO WATCH, LOOK, 
REPORT WHAT GOES ON, BOTH ON THE SURFACE, BELOW IT AND IN THE AIR. 

WE DO NOT STOP AND SEARCH SHIPS. WE ARE NOT DOING BLOCKADE DUTY. 

*IF WE GET A SURFACE CONTACT BY RADAR WE STEAM OVER AND GIVE HIV 
A VISUAL LOOK OVER. IF HE IS A MERCHANT SHIP WE ASK THE USUAL 
QUESTIONS ON OUR BLINKER (SHUTTERED SIGNAL SEARCHLIGHT) » WHO HE Is, 
HIS HOME PORT, WHERE FROM, WHERE BOUND AND WHAT HE CARRIES.® 

COCHRANE DID NOT SAY WHAT HE MIGHT DO IF A SHIP REFUSED TO ANSWER. 
NONE DID DURING MY WEEK ABOARD. 

WHILE THE DESTROYER HAS SIGHTED SEVERAL SIZABLE CONCENTRATIONS 
OF JUNKS AND SMALLER SANPANS» COCHRANE SAID HIS SHOULD HAS DETECTED 
NO MASSING OF JUNKS THAT WOULD INDICATE A RED INVASION BUILDUP, 

ON AN AVERAGE DAY A DESTROYER ON PATROL CONTACTS TWO OR THREE LARcE 
FREIGHTERS, FROM A HALF DOZEN TO SEVERAL HUNDRED JUNKS AND A SCORE 
OR MORE AIRCRAFT. THESE LAST ARE MOSTLY CHINESE NATIONALIST OR Ucs. 

IN RECENT WEEKS DESTROYERS ON NORTHERN PATROLS NEAR THE TACHENS 
HAVE BEEN MORE THAN THE USUAL FAST MOVING BLIPS NEAR THE MAINLAND, 
PROBABLY RED MIG JETS. 

IF MIGS OR OTHER RED PLANES HAVE COME CLOSE TO U.S. PATROL DESTROYERS 
THE NAVY ISN'T SAYING. BUT THERE IS AMPLE EVIDENCE THAT ANY RED 
PLANE THAT MANEUVERED INTO ATTACK POSITION WOULD GET A BARRAGE. THE 
DESTROYERS HAVE ORDERS TO DEFEND AGAINST THREATENED ATTACK.

BY GEORGE BOULTWOOD t 

BONN, GERMANY, FEBe7 (AP)-WEST GERMANY'S SOCIALIS 
POLL ON REARMAMENT TODAY IN EFFORT TO PROVE THEIR CONTENTGON pHRUDEtC 
NOST OF THEIR COUNTRYMEN ARE AGAINST IT. 

PARTY WORKERS BEGAN A DOOR-TO-DOOR SURVEY IN THE WIDELY 
VOTING DISTRICTS OF ASCHAFFENBURG, DORTMUND AND HOF. PERSONS OVES Ee 
18 WERE ASKED TO SIGN A MANIFESTO’CALLING FOR TALKS WITH RUSSIA OVER 
GERMAN REUNIFICATION BEFORE REARMAMENT. 

THE SOCIALISTS ALSO SET UP SPECIAL BOOTHS FOR PEOPLE TO REGISTER 
ANTI-ARMS VOTES. 

THE WEEKLONG POLL WAS PRECEDED BY A POSTER AND LEAFLET CAMPAIGN. 

IT MARKED A NEW PHASE IN THE BATTLE BETWEEN THE OPPOSITIION AND 
HANCELLOR KONRAD ADENAUER'S GOVERNMENT ON THE REARMAMENT QUESTION. 

ADENAUER AND HIS SUPPORTERS SAY WEST GERMAN MEMBERSHIP IN THE 
WORTH ATLANTIC ALLIANCE WILL EVENTUALLY LEAD TO REUNIFICATION. 

REFUSAL TO REARM WOULD EXPOSE WEST GERMANY TO THE DANGER OF BEING 
SWALLOWED UP AS A SOVIET SATELLITE, THEY CONTEND. 

A CONVENTION OF DISTRICT LEADERS OF ADENAUER'S CHRISTIAN DEMOCRATIC 
JNION GAVE FULL SUPPORT TO THIS VIEW YESTERDAY, PRESSING FOR SPEEDY 
RATIFICATION OF THE PARIS TREATIES AND PROMISING THAT EVERY EFFORT 
TO GET A CONFERENCE WITH THE RUSSIANS WOULD BE MADE AFTER WEST 
GERMANY REGAINS SOVEREIGNTY. 

SPEAKING TO THE MEETING, THE CHANCELLOR BITTERLY ATTACKED THE 
SOCIALIST POLL, SAYING SUCH TACTICS REMINDED HIM OF THE NAZIS BEFORE 
1933, HE SAID PARLIAMENT “AND NOT THE STREETS" MUST DECIDE ABOUT 
REARNAMENT 

ADDRESSING A RALLY OF 25,000 IN DORTMUND AS A CURTAIN-RAISER FOR 
THE POLL, SOCIALIST CHAIRMAN ERICH OLLENHAUER ARGUED NEGOTIATIONS 
WITH RUSSIA MUST BE GIVEN PRIORITY OVER REARMAMENT. HE ASSERTED THE 
DELAY IN FINAL FRENCH RATIFICATION OF THE PARIS TREATIES, EXPECTED 
BECAUSE OF THE FRENCH GOVERNMENT CRISIS, WOULD GIVE MORE TIME FOR AN 
APPROACH TO MOSCOW. 

ADENAUER IS STUMPING THE COUNTRY TO PUT HIS CASE TO THE PEOPLE 
BEFORE PARLIAMENT MAKES ITS SEMIFINAL VOTE ON THE PARIS PACTS

SALEM MADE THE STATEMENT AT A NEWS CONFERENCE FOR LEBANESE JOURNALISTS 


NOW VISITING EGYPT. LEADERS OF EIGHT ARAB STATES WOUND UP LAST NICHT 


A HEATED 16-DAY DEFENSE CONFERENCE=-CALLED BY EGYPT TO BLOCK THE IRAQI-

SALEM SAID THE ARAB WORLD IS NOW AT A CROSSROADS BUT DECLARED THE 
CRISIS IS NOT AN IRAQI-EGYPTIAN CONTEST FOR ARAB LEADERSHIP WAS SOME 
HAVE DESCRIBED IT. IT IS, HE SAID, A DEBATE TO AGREE ON UNIFIED ARAB 
POLICY ON MIDDLE EAST DEFENSE. 

WHILE IRAQ ADVOCATES FORMATION OF REGIONAL PACTS WITH FOREIGN 
COUNTRIES, EGYPT'S POLICY IS TO TRY TO STRENGTHEN THE ARAB SECURITY 
PACT AS A POWER CAPABLE OF DEFENDING THE MIDDLE EAST WITHOUT LOSING 
ARAB SOVEREIGNTY THROUGH LINKS WITH FOREIGN POWERS, SALEM SAID. . 

"BUT WE FAILED TO LEARN THE VIEWPOINTS OF OTHER ARAB STATES,” HE 
ADDED. “WE DID NOT LEARN WHETHER OTHER STATES WERE BACKING IRAQ OR 
EGYPT AND THAT IS WHY WE FAILED TO ANNOHNCE ANY STATEMENT AFTER THE 
CONFERENCE." 


THERE WERE INDICATIONS OTHER ARAB STATES IN ADDITION TO IRAQ WERE 
INCLINED EVENTUALLY TO JOIN UP WITH TURKEY, AND INDIRECTLY WITH THE 
WESTERN POWERS, BECAUSE OF THEIR GROWING FEAR OF POSSIBLE SOVIET 
AGGRESSION. 

EVEN SOME EGYPTIAN OFFICIALS ADMITTED PRIVATELY THE MEETING HAD 
BEEN A SHARP DEFEAT FOR EGYPT AND A BLOW AT HER LEADERSHIP OF THE 
LEAGUE. 

IT WAS A VICTORY FOR IRAQ'S TOUGH LITTLE ANTI-COMMUNIST PREMIER, 
NURI SAID, WHOSE CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES GAVE HIM A UNANIMOUS VOTE OF 
CONFIDENCE IN BAGHDAD LAST NIGHT AFTER HE SAID EMPHATICALLY HE WOULD 
COMPLETE THE DEFENSE TREATY WITH TURKEY IN SPITE OF EGYPT. 

NURI HAD REFUSED TO COME TO THE CAIRO MEETINGS, SAYING HE WAS 
ILLe HE BLUNTLY TOLD THE CONFERENCE DELEGATION WHICH FLEW TO BAGHDAD 
THAT IRAQ, AS A NEIGHBOR OF RUSSIA, MUST ALLY HERSELF WITH TURKEY 
BECAUSE THE ARAB STATES WERE TOO WEAK TO DEFEND THEMSELVES ALONE.

MALENKOV WAS IDENTIFIED IN THE PUBLIC MIND WITH THE CAMPAIGN TO 
CONCENTRATE ON LIGHT INDUSTRIES IN ORDER TO PRODUCE CONSUMER GOODS AND 
RAISE THE STANDARD OF LIVING OF THE SOVIET PEOPLE. 

THIS CONCENTRATION ON LIGHT INDUSTRIES WAS DENOUNCED RECENTLY 
AS CONTRARY TO THE TEACHINGS OF LENIN AND STALIN AND DANGEROUS FOR 
THE SOVIET STATE. MALENKOV, IN HIS RESIGNATION STATEMENT, SAID THE 
STATE MUST CONCENTRATE ON HEAVY INDUSTRY AS THE BASIS OF ALL 
PRODUCTION, PROSPEROUS AGRICULTURE AND DEFENSE.

LOBDONy FEBe 8 (AP)-THE FALL OF SOVIET PRIMER GEORGI MALENKOV 


BROUGHT UNEASY FOREBODINGS TO WESTERN EUROPEAN CAPITALS TONIGHT. 

PRIME MINISTER CHURCHILL TOLD THE HOUSE OF COMMONS: *THE 
FUTURE Is VEILED IN OBSCURITY." THAT WAS HIS ANSWER TO CALLS FOR 
A STA : 

WEST GERMAN CHANCELLOR KONRAD ADENAUER VIEWED THE MOSCOW 
DEVELOPMENTS, HOWEVER, AS A BOOST FOR THE BONN GOVERNMENT'S POLICY TO 
REARM WEST GERMANY WITHIN THE NORTH ATLANTIC TREATY ORGANIZATION. 

HE SAID MALENKOV'S FALL DEALT A DEVASTATING BLOW TO ANTI-REARMA- 
MENT GROUPS IN THE REPUBLIC, WHICH ARE HEADED BY THE SOCIALISTS. THE 
TIMING, HE TOLD A MASS MEETING OF HIS CHRISTIAN DEMOCRATIC PARTY IN 
FRANKFURT, COULD NOT HAVE BEEN BETTER TO ASSURE RATIFICATION OF THE 
PARIS ACCORDS. 

IN PARIS, FORMER FRENCH PREMIER GEORGES BIDAULT SAID: “THE 
DEPARTURE OF MALENKOV SHOULD SHOW THE WORLD THAT THE INSTABILITY 
OF WHICH FRANCE I$ ACCUSED ALSO EXISTS IN A TOTALITARIAN REGIME.” 

ITALIAN PREMIER MARIO SCELBA TOLD NEWSMEN IN ROMEs "I CAN ONLY 
EXPRESS MY HOPE THAT MALENKOV'S SUBSTITUTION WILL NOT MEAN THE 
WORSENING OF A POLICY UNDER THE MOTTO: ‘ALWAYS MORE CANNON. '" 

THE LONDON STOCK EXCHANGE DIPPED SLIGHTLY ON NEWS OF THE SOVIET 
CHANGE. THE RUSSIAN EMBASSY ANSWERED ALL TELEPHONE CALLS 
WITH? "WE HAVE NOTHING TO SAY." FOREIGN SECRETARY ANTHONY EDEN TOOK 
THE NEWS TO A MEETING OF BRITISH COMMONWEALTH PRIME MINISTERS. 

WORRY WAS REFLECTED IN SMALLER NATIONS.»

IN ADDITION TO THE ROMOSA PROBLEM, THE PRIME MINISTERS ALSO 
DISCUSSED REGIONAL DEFENSE MEASURES AND THE OVER-ALL STRATEGIC PROBLEMS 
OF THE FARFLUNG COMMONWEALTH. INDIA AND CEYLON STOOD ASIDE FROM THIS 
PHASE OF THE CONFERENCE BECAUSE THEY FOLLOW A NEUTRAL POLICY AND HAVE 
NO SECURITY PACT TIES. 

AMONG THE QUESTIONS BROUGHT UP WERE PLANS FOR FLYING "FIRE 
BRIGADE" TASK FORCES TO CHOKE OFF SMALL WARS THROUGHOUT THE 
COMMONWEALTH AND CHANGES IN DEFENSE PLANS NECESSARY BECAUSE OF ATOMIC 
ASPECTS OF ANY FUTURE WAR. 

THE PRIME MINISTERS ALSO CONSIDERED ADJUSTMENTS IN STRATEGIC THINKING 
MADE NECESSARY BY BRITAIN'S RECENT COMMITMENT TO KEEP FOUR DIVISIONS 
AND A TACTICAL AIR FORCE ON THE EUROPEAN CONTINENT AND BY BRITAIN'S 
WITHDRAWAL FROM THE SUEZ CANAL BASE. 

CREATION OF A BRITISH FLYING TASK FORCE SEEMED LIKELY TO BE PUT INTO 
OPERATION MORE QUICKLY AS A RESULT OF THE CONFERENCE. THE PLAN 
CALLS FOR A MOBILE RESERVE, PROBABLY OF TWO DIVISIONS, TO BE BUILT 
UP IN BRITAIN FROM FORCES BEING WITHDRAWN FROM THE MIDDLE EAST.

SINGAPORE, FEBsS (AUSTRALIAN FOREIGN MINISTER RICHARD Ge CASEY 
SAID TODAY THE FORTHCOMING SEATO CONFERENCE AT BANGKOK WILL BE 
CONCERNED MORE WITH COMBATING COMMUNIST SUBVERSION THAN WITH THE 
ALLOCATION OF A LARGE MILITARY FORCE FOR DEFENSE OF SOUTHEAST ASIA. 

CASEY ARRIVED BY AIR TODAY FROM SYDNEY. 

*I HAVE NO DOUBT THAT AT THE BANGKOK MEETING WE CAN TAKE A STEP 
FORWARD IN A MILITARY SPHERE," HE TOLD NEWSMEN. 

"AT THE SAME TIME THERE ARE THINGS THAT I SHOULD NOT EXPECT TO 
EMERGE. I DO NOT THINK THERE IS AN IMMEDIATE LIKLIHOOD OF A COMBINED 
FORCE BEING SENT UP OR OF A COMMANDER IN CHIEF BEING APPOINTED FOR THE 
REGION. I DO NOT SEE AS A RESULT OF THIS MEETING ANY LARGE FORCES 
BEING SENT IN THE NEAR FUTURE TO THE AREA. CONDITIONS DO NOT AT 
PRESENT EXIST WHICH WOULD MAKE SUCH THINGS POSSIBLE OR ACCEPTABLE 
TO THE MAJORITY OF THE SIGNATORIES.°

SOVIET REACTION (370) 
BY HAL COOPER 

LONDON, FEB. 9 (AP)-WEST EUROPE'S NON-COMMUNIST PRESS TOOK THE VIEW 
TODAY THAT THE NEW REGIME IN MOSCOW PRESAGES NEW. HARDSHIPS FOR THE 
SOVIET PEOPLE AND A STILL MORE UNYIELDING ATTITUDE TOWARDS THE WESTERN 

THIS WAS THE CONCLUSION THEY DREW FROM THE EMERGING DOMINANCE OF 
SOVIET COMMUNIST PARTY SECRETARY NIKITA Se KHRUSHCHEV, DESCRIBED BY THE 
-ABORITE LONDON DAILY HERALD AS "THE MAN WHO PUTS STEEL BEFORE BUTTER 
AND AMMUNITION BEFORE THE RUSSIAN PEOPLE'S APPETITES." 

SEVERAL WEST GERMAN NEWSPAPERS SAW GEORGI MALENKOV'S DEPARTURE FROM 
POWER AS A BLOW TO WESTERN HOPES OF NEGOTIATING AN END TO THE COLD WAR. 

SUPPORTERS OF WEST GERMAN REARMAMENT TOOK SOME COMFORT FROM THE 
SWITCH IN KREMLIN LEADERSHIP. CHANCELLOR KONRAD ADENAUER SAID IN A 
SPEECH IN FRANKFURT LAST NIGHT THAT MALENKOV'S FALL HAD BLIGHTED THE 
HOPES OF REARMAMENT'S FOES THAT THE SOVIETS WOULD COME TO TERMS ON 
GERMAN REUNIFICATION. 

LONDON'S LIBERAL NEWS CHRONICLE SAID MALENKOV'S DOWNFALL MAY SPEED 
THE RETIREMENT OF SIR WINSTON CHURCHILL, BRITAIN'S 80-YEAR-OLD PRIME 
MINISTER. 

CHURCHILL HAS DESCRIBED A LASTING PEACE AS “THIS LAST GREAT PRI 
I SFEK TO WIN." THE NEWS CHRONICLE SAID THE OLD MAN MAY “NOW DECIL 
THAT THE TIDE OF WORLD EVENTS IS RUNNING TOO FIERCELY AGAINST HIM 
AND BE RECONCILED TO RETIREMENT IN THE IMMEDIATE FUTURE." 

IN WEST GERMANY THE INDEPENDENT FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE WONDERED 
WHETHER THE WEST'S “SO-CALLED POLICY OF STRENGTH WAS NOT TOO MUCH 
BASED ON A NAIVE ASSUMPTION THAT THE RUSSIANS WERE SO PATIENT THEY WOULD 


REMAIN INDEFINITELY READY TO NEGOTIATE." 
"IT IS NOT IMPOSSIBLE THAT THIS PATIENCE HAS COME TO AN END NOW,” 


THE PAPER COMMENTED. 

THE INDEPENDENT FRANKFURTER RANDSCHAU AGREED: “THERE IS EVERY REASON 
TO REGRET THAT OPPORTUNITIES HAVE BEEN MISSED DURING THE TWO YEARS OF 
POST-STALIN POLICY." 

ITALIANS SPECULATED THAT THE CHANGE IN MOSCOW, MAY HAVE REPERCUSSIONS 
IN ITALY'S BIG COMMUNIST PARTY, WHOSE SECRETARY PALMIRO TOGLIATTI IS 
REGARDED AS A MODERATE OF MALENKOV'S STRIPE. IL QUOTIDIANO, VOICE OF 
THE ITALIAN CATHOLIC ACTION GROUP, SAID PERHAPS MALENKOV'.S FALL MEANS A 
POINT FOR FORMER DEPUTY PARTY SECRETARY PIETRO SECCHIA, WHO WAS DMOTED 
RECENTLY AMID RUMORS HE HAD INCITED THE FACTION'S TOUGH "ACTION Now" 


JING TO OPPOSE TOGLIATTI.

THIRD NIGHT LEAD FORMOSA TREATY 

WASHINGTON, FEB. 9 (AP)-THE SENATE, BY THE OVERWHELMING VOTE OF 64-¢ 
TONIGHT RATIFLED THE FORMOSA DEFENSE TREATY. 

THE PACT. SIGNED WITH THE CHINESE NATIONALIST REGIME OF CHIANG KAI- 
SHEK. COMMITS THE UNITED STATES TO DEFEND FORHOSA, CHIANG'S BASTION, 
AND THE NEARBY PESCADORES, AGAINST THE CHINESE REDS. 

THE SENATE VOTE WAS FAR IN EXCESS OF THE CONSTITUTIONAL REQUIREMENT 
THAAT TREATIES MUST OBTAIN APPROVAL OF TWO THIRDS OF THOSE VOTING. 

THE SENATE DECISION COMPLETED ACTION, SINCE TREATIES ARE NOT SUB- 
MITTED TO THE HOUSE. THE CHINESE HAVE ALREADY RATIFIED. 
TONIGHT’S VOTE WAS THE SECOND RECENT NOTICE TO THE CHINESE COMMUNISTS

REFUGEES (130) 

TAIPEI, FORMOSA, FEBs 11 (AP)-NATIONALIST CHINA TODAY ASKED THE 
UNITED STATES AND OTHER FRIENDLY COUNTRIES FOR "GENEROUS HELP® FOR 
THE CIVILIAN RESUGEES POURING INTO FORMOSA FROM THE TACHEN ISLANDS. 

FANG CHIH, IN CHARGE OF REFUGEE RELIEF WORK, SAID 16,067 CIVILIANS 
HAD REACHED FORMOSA FROM THE TACHENS AND ABOUT 2,500 MORE ARE EN 
ROUTE. SOME 2,000 MORE ARE DUE IN FROM NANCHISHAN. 

HE THANKED THE UsSe 7TH FLEET FOR ITS HELP IN TRANSPORTING 
THE REFUGEES TO FORMOSA, SAYING THIS DEMONSTRATED AGAIN THAT “ALL 
MEN ARE BROTHERS." 

FANG SAID THE REFUGEES WILL BE HOUSED FOR 10 DAYS IN 26 
RECEPTION CENTERS AT KEELUNG PORT IN NORTHERN FORMOSA. THEN THEY 
WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO FIVE OTHER CENTERS FOR THREE MONTHS FOR HELP 
TOWARD RESETTLEMENT. 

THE REFUGEES WILL BE GIVEN LOANS TO GET STARTED IN THEIR 
CHOICE OF WORKS FISHING, FARMING, STOCK RAISING AND HANDICRAFT.

BY JAMES De WHITE 
THE ASSOCIATED PRESS 
(FX) WHAT NEXT AFTER THE TACHENS? 
RED CHINA HAS THE INITIATIVE. 
PFIPING HAS MANY CHOICES. IT CAN SIT TIGHT AND SEE WHAT HAPPENS. 
IT CAN PICK OFF MORE OFFSHORE ISLANDS, PIECEMEAL, FROM NANCHISHAN TO 
SUEMOY. IT CAN BLOW THE WORKS AND GO AFTER FORMOSA. BUT SO MANY 
CHOICES ARE OPEN THAT IT'S ANYBODY'S GUESS WHAT PEIPING WILL DO NEXT. 
WHAT ARE THE MAIN FACTORS THAT MAY DETERMINE PEIPING'S STRATEGY? 
RED CHINA'S BASIC AIM IS TO BECOME THE DOMINANT POWER IN ASIA. 
THAT IS THE CLASSIC CHINESE CONCEPT OF CHINA'S PLACE IN THE WORLD. 
OVER THIS IS LAID THE DYNAMIC OF COMMUNISM, EVEN MORE AMBITIOUS. 
THE CLASSIC CHINESE IDEA OF HOW TO ATTAIN THIS GOAL IS THROUGH 


POLITICAL ACTION IN WHICH MILITARY ACTION IS USED AS A TOOL WHEN USEFUL, 


BUT ONLY AS A TOOL. 

THE CHINESE ARE NOT AFRAID TO USE THIS TOOL. THAT WAS SHOWN IN 
KOREA, WHERE IT PROFITED THEM UNDER THE CIRCUMSTANCES. THEY FOUGHT 
AND NEGOTIATED UseSe FORCES TO A STANDSTILL AND EMERGED WITH THE MOST 
POWERFUL COMBAT-TRAINED ARMY IN CHINESE HISTORY. 


THE CHINESE UNDOUBTEDLY REALIZE THAT NEXT TIME THE CIRCUMSTANCES WELL 


MAY NOT BE THE SAME. HERE WE GET INTO WHAT ACTUALLY IS THE CHINESE 
STATE OF MIND. THIS IS A COMPLEX WHICH HAS GROWN INCREASINGLY REMOTE 
TO THE WESTERN WORLD IN THE PAST FIVE YEARS OF RED RULE. 

MY ASIAN FRIENDS ASSURE ME OF TWO THINGS ABOUT THIS STATE OF 
MIND WHICH MAY BE OF SUPREME IMPORTANCE. 

ONE IS THE CHINESE CONVICTION THAT ANY WAR WITH THE UNITED STATES 
WOULD INVOLVE THE USE OF ATOMIC AND POSSIBLY HYDROGEN WEAPONS 
AGAINST THEM. WE USED THE ATOMIC BOMB ON JAPAN, WHY NOT ON CHINA? 


A4OF X 


THE OTHER IS AN EQUALLY FIRM CHINESE CONVICTION THAT THEY, IF ANYONE, 


CAN EMERGE FROM SUCH A WAR. THEY FIGURE IT THIS WAY: THEIR TREATY 
WITH RUSSIA GUARANTEES SOVIET INVOLVEMENT IN SUCH A WAR» RUSSIA 

AND THE UNITED STATES THEN WOULD DESTROY EACH OTHER'S WAR-MAKING 
POWERS» CHINA» WITH HER 600 MILLION PEOPLE AND EXPERIENCE IN SURVIVAL, 


RGE IF ANYONE DOES. 
WOUL NE. CHINESE MAY BE WRONG IN THESE CONVICTIONS, BUT MY. ASIAN FRIENDS 
ASSURE ME THEY HOLD THEM. 
THE OTHER SIDE OF THE COIN IS THIS QUESTIONS WHAT IF WAR DOES 
OP? 
NOT THAT CASE THE CHINESE CAN GO ON AS THEY ARE, EXERTING PRESSURE 
IN ALL DIRECTIONS, INCLUDING AGAINST RUSSIA, TO FURTHER THEIR OWN 


END IS IS THEIR CLASSIC FORMULA FOR SUCCESS, AND IT WORKS. THE 
OUTSTANDING EXAMPLE IS THE INDOCHINA SETTLEMENT. THE LATEST IS 
SUSSIA’S OPEN SUPPORT FOR RED CHINA'S CLAIM TO FORMOSA, WRUNG FROM 
RUSSIA AFTER THE CHINESE PAID LIP SERVICE TO RUSSIA'S COEXISTENCE 
POLICY AND SABOTAGED IT EXPERTLY THE WHILE. 

THIS MAY MEAN, AMONG OTHER THINGS, THAT THE CHINESE ARE NOT TO BE 
BOUGHT OFF WITH U.N. MEMBERSHIP AND DIPLOMATIC RECOGNITION. THE TIME 
TO HAVE EXTENDED THESE FAVORS, IF EVER, WAS WHILE THEY STILL WERE 
FAVORS--FIVE YEARS AGO WHEN CHINA WAS WEAK AND NEEDED THEM AND 
BEFORE SHE HAD ATTACHED HERSELF INSEPARABLY TO RUSSIA~ 

NOW, RED CHINA IS LIKE AN OUTLAW WHO HAS PROFITED BY PUTTING 
HIMSELF OUTSIDE THE LAW AND IS IN NO MOOD TO TAKE UP LAWFUL LIVING-- 


EXCEPT AT A VER

BALTIMORE. FEBs 11-(AP)-A HEARING AT WHICH JOHN DAVID PROVOO HoPEs 
TO BE FREED QF TREASON CHARGES RESUMED IN THE JUDGE'S CHAMBERS TODAY 
BUT ERUPTED INTO FEDERAL COURT WITH THE DISCLOSURE OF HERETOFORE SECRET 
REASONS WHY PROVOO WAS TRASNFERRED FROM MARYLAND TO NEW YORK BEFORE BEING 
CHA : 

AFTER 10 MINUTES IN THE CHAMBERS OF JUDGE ROSZEL Ce THOMSEN, 

THE HEARING WAS MOVED INTO THE COURTROOM. 

NOEL Ee STOREY, JUSTICE DEPARTMENT LAWYER, TESTIFIED*THE DECISION 
TO TRANSFER PROVOG FROM FT. MEADE, MD.»--WHERE HE WAS HELD ON ANOTHER 
CHARGE, TO FT.s JAY, NeYe, WHERE HE WAS GIVEN A DISHONORABLE DISCHARGE 
AND IMMEDIATELY ARRESTED’ BY THE FBI ON THE TREASON CHARGE--WAS REACHED 
IN A CONFERENCE AT THE PENTAGON ON AUG. 25, 1949. 

STOREY SAID THE ARMY WAS "ANXIOUS® TO GET RID OF PROVOO g FELT 
HE HAD BEEN HELD IN CUSTODY TOO LONG, AND WANTED TO GIVE HIM A MEDICAL 
D e 

HE SAID THE REASONS FOR THE JUSTICE DEPARTMENT WANTING TO GET HIM 
OUT OF THE MARYLAND FEDERAL COURT DISTRICT AND INTO NEW YORK WERES 

1. THE UsSe ATTORNEY IN BALTIMORE HAD BEEN "UNCOOPERATIVE" WITH 
THE DEPARTMENT ON CERTAIN MATTERS. ‘ ‘ 

2. "THE SENIOR JUDGE IN THE DISTRICT HAD SHOWN SOME ANTAGONISM 
TO DEPARTMENT LAWYERS WHO BROUGHT MATTERS HERE." : 

3. "WE CAN HOLD HIM (PROVOO) FOR A LONGER TIME IN NEW YORK BECAUSE 
THEY HAVE A MORE LIBERAL SETUP THERE AND FINISH INVESTIGATING BEFORE 
SEEKING AN INDICTMENT." 

STOREY SAID HIS TESTIMONY WAS BASED ON CONVERSATIONS HE REMEMBERED 
HAVING WITH ERNEST WHEARTEY, A JUSTICE DEPARTMENT OFFICIAL. 

DOCUMENTS CONCERNING THE TRANSFER AND THE REASONS FOR IT WERE MADE 
PART OF THE COURT RECORD. THEY HAD BEEN SUBPOENAED BY JUDGE THOMSEN 
LAST WEEK OVER THE OBJECTION OF UeSe ATTY. GEORGE COCHRAN DOUB, WHO

BY DAYBREAK THE BILLOWING EXPLOSIONS HAD CEASED AND AN EERIE SILENCE

THE EARLY MORNING TIDE EBBED ‘FOR THE FIRST TIME IN MANY CENTURIES 
WITH NO FISHERMEN SAILING WITH IT IN SEARCH OF FOOD. 

NO HEAVY INCENSE BURNED IN THE TACHEN TEMPLES. NO HOUSEWIVES 
HAGGLED WITH MERCHANTS AT THE MARKETS. NO ONE WAS BORN THERE TODAY.

: A 


WOREDYS NATIONS TODAY AGAINST "STICKING THEIR NOSES" INTO INTERNAL

X) 


SECOND LARGEST CITY, WHILE EN ROUTE HERE AFTTER A 73-DAY GOODWILL 
MISSION TO INDIA, BURMA AND EGYPT. - 

HE Is EXPECTED TO DELIVER A MAJOR ADDRESS LATER IN THE DAY IN 
BELG : 

TO HIS RAILSIDE AUDIENCE IN ZAGREB, TITO EXPLAINED THE REASONS 
FOR HIS MISSION. 

“THE MODERN WORLD," HE SAID, “IS A SINGLE UNIT AND IT IS VERY 
IMPORTANT THAT THERE ARE BROUGHT TOGETHER AS MANY AS POSSIBLE OF 
THOSE STATES AND PEOPLES WHO DESIRE TO PRESERVE PEACE AND 
INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION, WITHOUT REGARD TO THE DISTANCE BETWEEN 
THEM. 

TITO SAID THAT THERE "ARE STILL PEOPLE IN THE WORLD AND 
RESPONSIBLE STATESMEN WHO THINK THEY CAN INTERFERE IN INTERNAL AFFAIRS 
OF COUNTRIES. 

*THE ASIAN COUNTRIES I HAVE VISITED, AND PROBABLY OTHERS AS WELL, 
ARE THINKING THAT THE TIME OF FOREIGN {NTERFENCE HAS ENDED. IT 
SHOULD BE TIME FOR THOSE WHO DESIRE TO INTERFERE IN INTERNAL 
AFFAIRS OF OTHER COUNTRIES TO STICK THEIR NOSES INTO THEIR OWN 
DOMESTIC PROBLEMS INSTEAD OF STICKING THEM INTO THE AFFAIRS OF OTHER 
COUN Se 

HE ASSERTED THAT THE NATIONS OF THE WORLD MUST LEARN TO COEXIST IN 
ORDER TO PRESERVE WORLD PEACE." 

YUGOSLAVIA'S CHIEF OF STATE SAID THAT "THE ACTIVE COEXISTENCE 
(BETWEEN NATIONS) IS POSSIBLE IF THERE IS NO INTERFERENCE IN OTHER 
“OUNTRIES’ DOMESTIC AFFAIRS. IF SOMEONE WANTS DOMINATION, THEN A 
“ONFLICT IS INEVITABLE." 

IN A TEN-MINUTE ADDRESS, HE CONCENTRATED CHIEFLY UPON THE RESULTS 
)F HIS TRIP AND AN OPTIMISTIC FORECAST OF FRUITFUL TRADE RELATIONS 
SFTWEEN YUGOSLAVIA AND THE MID-EAST ON A BASIS OF “EQUALITY.

\NYONE’S SATELLITES BUT WISH TO BE INDEPENDENT

NIGHT LEAD NIXON 

MEYER 

A, FEB. 12 (AP) -CHEERING THRONGS GREETED VICE PRESIDENT 
ON TODAY AS HE ARRIVED IN GUATEMALA ON HIS CARIBBEAN GOOD 
WILL TOURe HE WAS WELCOMED AT THE AIRPORT BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE 
CONGRESS, LUIS GONZALEZ, AND HIGH GUATEMALAN OFFICIALS« 

IN RESPONSE TO THE WELCOME, NIXON SAID: 

“YOU HAVE WON THE ADMIRATION OF THE PEOPLE OF THE WORLD FOR THE 
WAY YOUR HEROIC PEOPLE OVERTHREW COMMUNISM. YOU ALSO GAVE HOPE TO 
FNSLAVED PEOPLES ALL OVER THE WORLD FOR YOUR BRAVERY." 

WITH THE VICE PRESIDENT'S ARRIVAL THERE WERE SIGNS HE WOULD URGE 
AN IMMEDIATE STEP-UP IN THE UNITED STATES ECONOMIC AID PROGRAM TO 
THIS LITTLE REPUBLIC WHICH OUSTEDTHE COMMUNIST-SUPPORTED REGIME OF 
FX-PRESIDENT JACOBO ARBENZ GUZMAN IN A REVOLUTION LAST JUNE. 

THE COUNTRY HAS RECEIVED ONLY SLIGHTLY MORE THAN SIX MILLION 
DOLLARS IN HELP AND IT WAS LEARNED AUTHORITATIVELY THAT NIXON Is 
FAGER TO GET WASHINGTON MOVING TO AVOID AN ECONOMIC COLLAPSE HERE. 

THE AIRPORT AND CITY STREETS WERE DRAPED WITH FLAGS AND BUNTING. 
A TYPICAL MARIMBA BAND PLAYED AS THE VICE PRESIDENT AND HIS WIFE 
STEPPED FROM PRESIDENT EISENHOWER'S FORMER PERSONAL PLANE, THE 

MBINE Ile 
COL UATEMALANS IN BRILLIANTLY COLORED NATIVE COSTUMES CHEERED AND 
WAVED AS THE NIXONS RODE IN AN OPEN CAR THROUGH GREAT AVENUES OF 
CYPRESS TREES AND FLAMING BOUGANVILLA. 

ORESIDENTIAL HORSEGUARDS PRECEDED THE MOTORCADE. MANY IN THE 
CROWDS ALONG THE ROUTE REACHED OUT AND SHOOK HANDS WITH BOTH THE 
VICE PRESIDENT AND HIS WIFE.

DECLARED TODAY THAT "IN NO CASE" WOULD THE STRATEGIC ISLANDS OF QUEMOY 
AND MALSU BE ABANDONED. HE INDICATED STRONGLY HE EXPECTS THE 
UNITED STATES TO JOIN IN THEIR DEFENSE. 

THE CHINESE NATIONALIST PRESIDENT, STILL SMARTING FROM THE LOSS OF 
THE TACHEN ISLANDS WITHOUT A FIGHT, WAS ASKED AT A PRESS CONFERENCE 
IF THE UNITED STATES WOULD JOIN NATIONALIST CHINNESE IN DEFENSE OF 
THESE ISLANDS IF THEY ARE ATTACKED.

*WITH REGARD TO THE QUESTION OF THE JOINT DEFENSE OF THE OFFSHORE

FLUCIDATIONs

MILITARY EXPERTS. |

COPENHAGEN, DENMARK, FEB. 15 -A HEFTY ROMANIAN GIRL TODAY 
DENOUNCED HER’ HUSBAND AS A "CRIMINAL BANDITTO" AND TRAITOR FOR TAKING 
DERRENCY WORTH $850 FROM THE ROMANIAN LEGATION AND SEEKING POLITICAL 
ASYLYM. “I COULD KILL HIM IF WE/EVER MEET AGIN," SHE SAID. 

THE GIRL, MRS» MARIA CIMPU WAS MARRIED EIGHT MONTHS AGO TO IoN 
CIMPU, 24, DESCRIBED BY THE LEGATION AS A HANDYMAN AND PART-TIME 
CNAUFREUR, HE ASKED POLIC SATURDAY FOR POLITICAL ASYLYM IN DENMARK AND 
CID HE FEARED HIS WIFE MIGHT BE FORCED AGAINST HER WILL TO RETURN TO 
SNEIR COMMUNIST-RULED HOMELAND, ROMANIAN CHARGE D'AFFAIRES ALEXANDRO 
GHIRILA ARRANGED FOR NEWSMEN TO MEET MRS.» CIMPU TODAY AT THE 
LEGATION IN AN EFFORT TO DISPROVE HER HUSBAND'S CHARGE. 

MRS CIMPU APPEARED NERVOUS AS SHE TWISTED A PIECE OF RUBBER BAND WITH 
HANDS RED AND SWOLLEN FROM DISHWASHING AND KITCHEN WORK. BUT 
MERE WAS NOTHING TO INDICATE SHE WAS BEING HELD AGAINST HER WILL OR 
WAS. NOT SPEAKING FREELY. ON THE OTHER HAND THERE WAS NO PROOFgQec 
SHE HAD NOT BEEN COAcHED FOR TODAY'S CONFERENCE. A HEAVY GUARD 1955 
OF DANISH UNIFORMED POLICE AND INTELLIGENCE AGENTS SURROUND THE 
LEGATION TO MAKE SURE MRS. CIMPU IS NOT SPIRITED AWAY TO ROMANIA, 

THE POLICE SAY THEY ARE NOT SURE SHE IS ACTING OF HER OWN FREE WILL. 

BUT MRS» CIMPU APPEARED GENUINELY ANGRY WITH HER HUSBAND AS SHE 
ANSWERED NEWSMEN'’S QUESTIONS READILY. / 

®I HAVE LOVED ION WITH ALL MY HEART,” SHE SAID, “BUT MY LOVE Is 
DEAD AFTER WHAT HE HAS DONE. 

®wE HAVE KNOWN EACH OTHER FOR 12 MONTHS AND BEEN MARRIED FOR EIGHT. 
WE WERE VERY HAPPY WHEN WE CAME HERE FOUR MONTHS AGO. I DON'T SEE HIM 
ANY MORE. HE IS A TRAITOR TO OUR NATION, AND HE HAS BETRAYED OUR 
LOVE. I COULD KILL HIM IF WE EVER MEET AGAIN." 

ASKED ABOUT EFFORTS BY THE DANISH FOREIGN MINISTRY TO ARRANGE A 
MEETING BETWEEN THE COUPLE TO GIVE MRS. CIMPU A CHANCE TO JOIN HER 
HUSBAND, SHE AND CHIRILA SAID SUCH A MEETING WAS OUT OF THE QUESTION.

THE RANCHING AND MINING DISTRICT IN EAST CENTRAL NEVADA BETWEEN 
CALIENTE AND PIOCHE. THE AREA LIES ABOUT 165 MILES NORTHEAST OF 
LAS VEGAS AND LESS THAN 90 MILES FROM THE YUCCA FLAT TEST SITE. 

SIMILAR WINDS BLEW BRISKLY TODAY BUT SKIES WERE CLEAR AND SUNNY. 

CIVIL DEFENSE PROJECTS WILL PLAY A MAJOR ROLE IN THE FIRST TEST AND 
THROUGHOUT THE SERIESe CHAIRMAN LEWIS LeSTRAUSS OF THE AEC, WHO TODAY 
RELEASED FULL DETAILS ON THE H-BOMB'S RADIATION POTENTIAL» HAS 
INDICATED THAT CIVIL DEFENSE AGAINST ALL NUCLEAR AND THERMONUCLEAR 
WEAPONS IS NOW UPPERMOST IN GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS’ THINKING. 

THE FIRST PROJECTS, IT IS BELIEVED, WILL BE LARGELY BIOMEDICAL AND 
RADIOLOGICAL IN NATURE. NO ANIMALS WILL BE EXPOSED TO THE FIRST SHOT, 
ALTHOUGH RATS WILL BE PUT IN SHELTERS IN A FUTURE TEST. IT HAS NOT 
BEEN DISCLOSED WHETHER STRUCTURES WILL BE BLASTED IN THE OPENER». — —

INDONESIA, FEB« 17 (AP)-PREMIER CHOU EN-LAI ACCEPTING 


LAKART A 
AN INVIITATION TODAY COMMUNIST CHINA TO ATTEND THE ASIAN-AFRICAN 
CONFERENCE, DECLARED HE SAW NO REASON WHY NATIONS WITH DIFFERENT 
FORMS OF GOVERNMENT COULDN'T "COEXIST IN PEACE.” 

THE CONFERENCE SECRETARIAT SAID CHINA'S FORMAL ACCEPTANCE CAME 
WITH CHOU'S PRAISES OF THE CONFERENCE AS “THE FIRST OF ITS KIND IN 
HISTORY CONVENED TO PROMOTE GOODWILL AND COOPERATION AMONG THE 
COUNTRIES OF ASIA AND AFRICA." 

CHOU SAID THE CONFERENCE "ACCORDS A GOOD OPPORTUNITY FOR ENABLING 
ASIAN AND AFRICAN COUNTRIES WITH DIFFERENT SOCIAL SYSTEMS TO COEXIST 
IN PEACE UNDER THE PRINCIPLE THAT THE FORM OF GOVERNMENT AND WAY OF 
LIFE OF ANY ONE COUNTRY SHOULD IN NO WAY BE SUBJECT TO INTERFERENCE 


BY ANOTHER.” 

CHOU DECLARED THE CONFERENCE “REFLECTS THE EVER STRONGER DESIRE 
OF ASIAN AND AFRICAN COUNTRIES TO TAKE THEIR DESTINY INTO THEIR OWN 
HANDS AND TO ENTER ON AN EQUAL FOOTING INTO FRIENDLY COOPERATION 


WITH THE OTHER COUNTRIES OF THE WORLD." 
HE SAID RED CHINA AGREES WITH THE CONFERENCE AIMS BUT IS NOT 


YET ABLE TO ANNOUNCE THE SIZE OF ITS DELEGATION. 
THE TALKS ARE TO BE HELD IN THE WEST JAVA MOUNTAIN CITY OF 

BANDUNG APRIL 18-24. ACCEPTANCES HAVE COME ALSO FROM THAILAND, 

ETHIOPIA, COMMUNIST VIET NAM, IRAQ AND EGYPT. 


LIBYA, AFGHANISTAN

LONDON, FEB.s18 (AP) -HERMANN FIELD SAID TODAY HE SPENT FIVE 
VEARS IMPRISONED IN A CELLAR IN COMMUNIST POLAND, AND DISCLOSED THE 
eeeaW GOVERNMENT HAS PAID HIM $50,000 FOR WRONGFUL ARREST. 

HE INSISTED HE IS AT A LOSS TO EXPLAIN THE CASE OF THE 
DISAPPEARING FIELDS," AND SAID HE WAS NEVER A COMMUNIST OR “AN 
AGENT FOR ANYBODY." 

“I AM NOT A COMMUNIST AND NEVER WAS ONE," HE SAID. “OVER THE 
COURSE OF 20 YEARS I HAVE OCCASIONALLY AGREED WITH SOME OF THE 
POLICIES FOR WHICH THE COMMUNIST PARTY SAID IT STOOD. FOR INSTANCE, 
I WAS VERY MUCH OPPOSED TO THE RISE OF HITLER AND WAS OPPOSED TO 
THE OCCUPATION OF CZECHOSLOVAKIA BY GERMAN FORCES.® 

THE 44-YEAR-OLD CLEVELAND ARCHITECT APPEARED AT A LONDON NEWS 
CONFERENCE 24 HOURS AFTER HIS ARRIVAL FROM A REST PERIOD IN 
SWITZERLAND. POLAND RELEASED HIM IN OCTOBER. 

FOUR MEMBERS OF THE FIELD FAMILY DISAPPEARED BEHIND THE IRON 
CURTAIN IN 1949. HERMANN’S OLDER BROTHER, NOEL, A FORMER U.S. 
STATE DEPARTMENT OFFICIAL, AND HIS WIFE WERE RELEASED RECENTLY FROM 
A HUNGARIAN PRISON AND CHOSE TO STAY IN HUNGARY. NOEL'S ADOPTED 
DAUGHTER, ERICA WALLACH, HAS BEEN REPORTED IN EXILE IN SIBERIA.

BONN, GERMANY, FEB. 18 (AP)-TWO OF THE FOUR PARTIES IN CHANCELLOR 
KONRAD ADENAUER'$ COALITION GOVERNMENT CALLED TODAY FOR CREATION OF 


A PERMANENT COMMISSION TO PREPARE PLANS FOR REUNITING GERMANY. 
IN A RESOLUTION SUBMITTED TO THE BUNDESTAG (LOWER HOUSE) 
THE FREE DEMOCRATS (FDP) AND THE GERMAN PARTY (DP) SAID "THE 

GERMAN PEOPLE EXPECT THAT THE GREAT POWERS WILL TAKE ALL 
NECESSARY MEASURES TO RESTORE A UNITED GERMANY." 

THE RESOLUTION CALLS ON THE BUNDESTAG TO URGE EARLY FOUR 
POWER NEGOTIATIONS TOs 

1. PREPARE THE ELECTION OF AN ALL-GERMAN PARLIAMENT AND 
A NATIONAL GERMAN GOVERNMENT. 

2. DEVELOP A CONSTITUTION FOR ALL GERMANY. 


* 


3. ARRANGE FOR INTE ONAL PROTECTION OF A UNITED: GERM 
THE RESOLUTION SAID THe FIRST STEP TOWARD THIS GOAL SHOULD Ke 
THE FORMATION OF THE JOINT COMMISSION, MADE UP OF REPRESENTATIVEs 
FROM BRITAIN, FRANCE, THE SOVIET UNION, THE UNITED STATES AND 
WEST GERMANY.

WASHINGTON, FEB. 18 (AP)-NEXT ON THE LIST OF OFFSHORE ISLANDS THE 
CHINESE REDS WANT TO WREST FROM GENERALISSIMO CHIANG KAI-SHEK MAY BE 
TINY, ROCK RIDGED NANCHI, SOUTH OF THE ABANDONED TACHENS. 
THIS DEFINITE POSSIBILITY WAS BEING CONSIDERED IN WASHINGTON TONIGHT. 
WHATEVER MILITARY OR PSYCHOLOGICAL FACTORS MIGHT BE INVOLVED, AN 
OVERT MOVE AGAINST NANCHI WOULD PRESENT A NEW HOUR OF DECISION FOR THE 
UNITED STATES--THE NECESSITY OF EITHER GOING TO ITS DEFENSE, AGAIN 
COVERING REMOVAL OF NATIONALIST TROOPS AND CIVILIANS AS WAS DONE IN THE 
CASE OF TACHEN, OR OF SIMPLY STANDING BACK AND LETTING THE REDS SEIZE 
ISLAND»

DES MOINES, FEB 19-(AP)-SIR ROGER MAKINS, BRITISH AMBAS 

SADG ROTO. THE UNITED STATES, INDICATED TONIGHT THAT BRITAIN REGARDS THE 

PROBLEM OF FORMOSA'S STATUS AS ONE WHICH POSSIBLY CAN BE SETTLED BY 

DIPLOMATIC NEGOTIATION. 


* VIEWS WERE EXPRESSED IN REMARKS PREPARED FOR THE CLOSING 
ADDRESS. TO THE NATIONAL FARM INSTITUTE, AN ANNUAL FORUM SPONSORED BY THE 
DES MOINES CHAMBER OF COMMERCE. THIS YEAR'S THEME WAS “THE FARMER 
AND THE FREE SOCIETY." UeSe ATTYs GEN» HERBERT BROWNELL WAS SCHEDULED 


ER WITH MAKINS. ED 
- SROWNELL. vag UNABLE TO REACH DES MOINES BECAUSE BAD WEATHER GROUND 


HIS AIRPLANE IN DETROIT. HE RETURNED TO WASHINGTON. 


“IS NOT 
' D THE BRITISH APPROACH TO INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS “I 
sPESTRCULAR® Sat THAT IT FREQUENTLY IS SUCCESSFUL. HE MENTIONED AS 
oP EMPLES IN THE LAST 12 MONTHS “THE SETTLEMENT OF DIFFICULT AND OF 
EATTER DISPUTES WITH IRAN, WITH EGYPT AND IN. TRIESTE." 
HE DISCUSSED BRITAIN'S ANSWER TO THE “THREAT TO FREEDOM" AND 
ASSERTED THAT THIS THREAT “CONSISTS IN THE TWINCOMMUNIST AMBITIONS 
OF IMPERIALISM AND SUBVERSION." 
“THE BRITISH," HE SAID, ®BELIEVE THAT, GIVEN TIME AND 
PATIENCE, INTERNATIONAL DIFFERENCES, HOWEVER ACUTE, CAN. WITH THE 
MINIMUM OF GOODWILL ON THE OTHER SIDE, BE SETTLED BY NEGOTIATIONee. 
WE LIKE TO SETTLE ONE PROBLEM AT A TIME, RATHER THAN ATTEMPT A GENERAL 
SOLUTION. WE DO NOT EXPECT QUICK RESULTS. 
"WE RECOGNIZE THAT SOME PROBLEMS MAY HAVE TO BE LEFT OVER FOR LATER 
SOLUTION AND THAT WE MAY HAVE TO GET ALONG FOR A TIME WITH SOME 
RATHER UNTIDY "MODUS VIVENDI." THE STATUS OF FORMOSA, SO MUCH IN OUR 
MINDS ODAY, IS JUST SUCH A PROBLEM.® 
THE BRITISH AMBASSADOR, REFERRING TO WHAT HE CALLED “A SCOWLING 
SOVIET UNION AND A CHINA WHICH THREATENS TO RAMPAGE," SAID: 
*"WE BELIEVE THE «e+e POLICY OF FIRMNESS COMBINED WITH A READINESS 
TO NEGOTIATE--IN THREE WORDS, PEACE THROUGH STRENGTH--CAN STILL BE 
ON INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIC PROBLEMS, SIR ROGER SIAD THE BRITISH 
ARE ANXIOUS *FOR CARE AND CONSULTATION IN THE TRICKY PROBLEM OF THE 
DISPOSAL OF YOUR GREAT AGRICULTURAL SURPLUSES." 
HE SAID NATIONS IN THE STERLING BLOC HOPE TO MAKE FURTHER PROGRESS 
IN 1955 TOWARD THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF MAKING THEIR CURRENCY CONVERTIBLE 
BUT WARNED "THIS CAN ONLY BE DONE IF TRADE IS FREER" BECAUSE “TRADE 
AND FINANCE GO HAND IN HAND.®

ON SEVERAL OCCASIONS LAST FALL AND THIS WINTER HIGH RANKING SOVIET 
OFFICIALS, INCLUDING KHRUSHCHEV, HAVE "EXPLAINED" TO THE PUBLIC THEY 
COULD EXPECT SHORTAGES IN SOVIET STORES OF SOME GOODS, 

' THEY APPARENTLY WERE RIGHT. 

THE FACT REMAINS THAT NO MATTER HOW MUCH "EXPLANATION" THERE IS THE 
SHORTAGES ARE NOT CALCULATED TO MAKE RUSSIANS ANY HAPPIER. IN THE 
PRESENT POLITICAL SITUATION IN RUSSIA SUCH THINGS CAN BE IMPORTANT 
POLITICALLY. THOSE WHO STUDY RUSSIAN HISTORY» INCLUDING THE KREMLIN 
LEADERS, KNOW THAT OONE OF THE FACTORS IN STARTING THE REVOLUTION WHICH 
OVERTHREW THE TSAR IN 1917 WAS A FOOD SHORTAGE IN PETROGRAD (NOW 
LENINGRAD). THE FACT THAT FORMER PREMIER MALENKOV BLAMED HIMSELF FOR 
FARM FAILURES IN THE RESIGNATION STATEMENT READ FOR HIM FEB. 8, AND THE 
ADDITIONAL FACT THAT ONE OF THE CHIEF CHARGES AGAINST EXECUTED FORMER 
POLICE CHIEF LAVRENTY BERIA WAS THAT HE SABOTAGED FARM AND FOOD 
POLICIES, SHOW HOW ACUTELY CONSCIOUS OF THIS SUBJECT THE SOVIET 
GOVERNMENT IS. 

THIS IS ONE OF THE FACETS OF THE SITUATION IN WHICH THE UsS. 
GOVERNMENT IS CONSIDERING MAKING A WHEAT GIFT TO RUSSIA. SECRETARY OF 
AGRICULTURE BENSON TODAY SAID HE HAS TALKED WITH PRESIDENT EISENHOWER 
ABOUT THIS PROJECT AND THAT THE IDEA HAS NOT BEEN DROPPED. 

THOSE WHO ADVOCATE IT SAY IT WOULD GIVE A DEMONSTRATION TO THE 
RUSSIAN PEOPLE, AS DISTINCT FROM THEIR RULERS, OF THE FRIENDSHIP OF 
AMERICA, AND THAT IT WOULD FORCE SOVIET LEADERS TO MAKE A DIFFICULT 
CHOICE’ “EITHER TO REFUSE THE GIFT AND INCUR POSSIBLE DISPLEASURE FROM

* BONN GERMANY, FEB. 21 (AP)-CHANCE 


EXPECTED TO CALL ON THE WESTERN POWER 


FOR A BIG-POWER CONFERENCE EVEN BEFORE WEST GERMANY STARTS 
REARMING UNDER THE PARIS TREATIES. | 

FOREIGN DIPLOMATS AND GERMAN POLITICAL LEADERS BELIEVE HE IS 
PLANNING THIS STEP IN VIEW OF THE MOUNTING HOME FRONT PRESSURE FOR 
UNIFICATION AND THE DEEPENDING RIFT AMONG WEST GERMANS OVER 


REARMAMENT. 
ADENAUER, 79, HAS NOT PUBLICLY COMMITTED HIMSELF ON THE TIMING 
OF NEW EAST-WEST TALKS. HIS GOVERNMENT SAYS ONLY: "WE ARE IN 


CONTINUOUS CONTACT WITH THE WESTERN POWERS ON THE QUESTION OF A NEW 
CONFERENCE ON THE GERMAN QUESTION.” 
ADENAUER HAS SAID CAUTIOUSLY THAT 


IN HIS RECENT PUBLIC UTTERANCES 
HELD" AFTER RATIFICATION OF THE REARMA- 


TALKS WITH THE RUSSIANS "COULD BE 
MENT TREATIES.» 

REJECTING THE OPPOSITION SOCIALISTS’ DEMAND FOR TALKS BEFORE THE 
TREATIES GO INTO EFFECT, HE HAS SAID SUCH NEGOTIATIONS WOULD BE 
"SENSELESS" FROM THE GERMAN STANDPOINT BEFORE THE BONN REPUBLIC RECEIVES 
SOVEREIGNTY UNDER THESE PACTS. : 

OFFICIALS CLOSE TO ADENAUER SAY HE WANTS EQUAL GERMAN PARTICIPATION 
WITH THE OTHER WESTERN POWERS IN PREPARATION OF NEW EAST-WEST TALKS 
AND PERHAPS IN THE CONFERENCE ITSELF. HE THEREFORE FEELS THAT 
RESTORATION OF SOVEREIGNTY. UNDER THE TREATIES WILL BE EVEN MORE 
IMPORTANT FOR GERMANS THAN THE RIGHT TO REARM. 

ADENAUER IS SAID TO BELIEVE THE TREATIES WILL BE RATIFIED FINALLY 
IN MARCH AND WEST GERMANY WILL BECOME A SOVEREIGN STATE BY APRIL 1. 
IF THIS HAPPENS, THE WEST GERMANS COULD START REARMING WITHIN A FEW 
MONTHS PROVIDED THE NECESSARY ENABLING LEGISLATION IS NOT DELAYED IN 
PARLIAMENT OR THE COURTS.

MATUSOW TESTIFIED THAT HE HAD TOLD THE TRUTH WHEN HE SIGNED AN AFFI- 
DAVIT IN SEPTEMBER 1953 RECANTING HIS PREVIOUS STATEMENTS THAT HE KNEW 
OF "126 COMMUNISTS ON THE STAFF OF THE NEW YORK TIMES.” 

HE SAID HIS RECOLLECTION IS THAT HE SAID IN THE AFFIDAVIT “I DID Nor 
KNOW OF MORE THAN FOUR OR FIVE" BUT HE LATER IDENTIFIED A COPY OF THE 
AFFIDAVIT WHICH PLACED THE NUMBER AT SIX. 

MATUSOW SAID HE NOW CAN RECALL THE NAME OF ONLY ONE, AND ONLY THE 
LAST NAME. SAID HE IS “QUITE CONFIDENT® THAT MAN 18 A MR. FISHER, 
BUT DID NOT SPELL THE NAME. HE ADDED THAT HE DOES NOT RECALL 


WHETHER HE GAVE OTHER NAMES TO THE TIMES. 
SOURWINE ASKED MATUSOW WHETHER THE TIMES GAVE HIM “$500 IN EXHCNAGE 


FOR THE AFFIDAVIT." 

"NO, SIR,° MATUSOW REPLIED. HE SAID THE TIMES WIRED HIM $300 AT 
RENO, hev..’TO PAY HIS EXPENSES OF TRAVELING TO LOS ANGELES WHERE HE 
SAIB’HE DICTATED AND SIGNED THE AFFIDAVIT BEFORE A NOTARY PUBLIC. HE 
SAID THE TIMES SPECIFIED THAT HE SHOULD RETURN ANY OF THE $300 NOT 
SPENT FOR ACTUAL EXPENSES. 

MATUSOW SAID HE DID NOT RETURN ANY BALANCE BECAUSE "MY MONEY WAS 
STOLEN AT THE HOTEL" WHERE HE STAYED.

W e 25 (AP)-THE NEWS FROM MOSCOW INDICATES THE KREMLIN 

BOSSES NIKITA KHRUSHCHEV AND PREMIER NIKOLAI BULGANIN ARE GIVING A 
QUICKIE BUILDUP TO BALD WAR HERO MARSHAL IVAN KONEV. 

THEY APPARENTLY WANT TO MAKE HIM A POLITICAL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THEIR 
POPULAR DEFENSE MINISTER MARSHAL GEORGI ZHUKOV. 

OBSERVERS OF SOVIET AFFAIRS DRAW THIS CONCLUSION FROM THE UNUSUAL 
PROMINENCE WHICH KONEV HAS BEEN GETTING EVER SINCE FEBe 8. THAT WAS 
THE DAY GEORGI MALENKOV "RESIGNED® AS PREMIER AND BULGANIN WAS NAMED 


HIS a etiien RY SmUKON HIS PREVIOUS JOB AS DEFENSE MINISTER VACANT 


TO BE FILLED BY ZHUKOV THE NEXT DAY. 

ZHUKOV HAS BEEN MUCH IN THE SPOTLIGHT SINCE THEN. HIS INTERVIEW 
WITH THREE AMERICAN NEWSMEN WAS PUBLISHED IN MAJOR SOVIET PAPERS. 
LAST NIGHT HE SPOKE FOR SOVIET ARMY DAY IN THE BOLSHOI THEATRE. TODAY 
HE ISSUED AN ORDER OF THE DAY. 

BUT PARALLEL WITH ZHUKOV'S INCREASED PUBLICITY, MARSHAL KONEV HAS 
ALSO BEEN GIVEN A SHARE IN THE LIMELIGHT. 

ON FEB. 9 KONEV SPOKE IN THE SOVIET PARLIAMENT, THE SUPREME SOVIET. 
THIS WAS SIGNIFICANT IN VIEW THAT SOVIET CAREER MARSHALS, AS 
DISTINCT FROM THE POLITICAL MARSHALS SUCH AS BULGANIN, RARELY HAVE 
SPOKEN IN THIS ASSEMBLAGE. KONEV IN HIS ADDRESS MADE CLEAR HE WAS. 
SPEAKING FOR THE ARMED FORCES. HE TOOK A BELLIGERENT TONE. ws5 

TODAY KONEV IN A MAJOR ARTICLE IN PRAVDA PRAISED KHRUSHCHEV AND 
BULGANIN AND THE CENTRAL COMMITTEE OF THE COMMUNIST PARTY--OF WHICH 
HE IS A MEMBER. 

IT LOOKS AS THOUGH KONEV IS BEING USED BY THE KHRUSHCHEV- 
BULGANIN GROUP AMONG THE KREMLIN POLITICIANS AS A SORT OF WARNING 
TO ZHUKOV NOT TO REACH TOO FAR. 

KONEV, THOUGH A CAREER MILITARY MAN, HAS BEEN INVOLVED IN SOVIET 
POLITICS UP TO HIS NECK BEFORE THIS. AE HAS BEEN USED AGAINST 
ZHUKOV BEFORE. STALIN NAMED KONEV COMMANDER OF SOVIET LAND FORCES 
AFTER THE WAR--REPLACING ZHUKOV WHO WAS SENT TO EXILE AS COMMANDER OF 
A SOUTHERN MILITARY DISTRICT.

ANDREI GROMYKO TO SPELL OUT RUSSIA'S DISARMAMENT PROPOSALS IN DETALL 

CHURCHILL'S STATEMENT WAS READ TO THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AS THE 
DELEGATES OF BRITAIN, RUSSIA,THE UNITED STATES, FRANCE AND CANADA 
GATHERED FOR THE RESUMED SESSION OF THE UeNe DISARMAMENT SUBCOMMITTEE. 

STRESSING THAT THE SUBCOMMITTEE'S DELIBERATIONS WILL BE SECRET, 
CHURCHILL SAID: 

“I FEEL SURE, IN THE INTEREST OF INTERNATIONAL AGREEMENT, THAT THIS 
IS THE BEST METHOD OF DISCUSSING THESE ISSUES. IF THIS COULD BE ACHI- 
EVED, A WORLD CONFERENCE WOULD BE POSSIBLE AND NECESSARY." 

CHURCHILL WAS REPLYING TO LABORITE HECTOR HUGHES, WHO ASKED WHAT 
THE BRITISH ATTITUDE WAS TO RUSSIA'S FEB. 18 DISARMAMENT PROPOSALS. 
THESE CALLED FOR A WORLD DISARMAMENT CONFERENCE IN CONJUNCTION WITH 
ABOLITION OF ALL STOCKS OF ATOMIC AND HYDROGEN WEAPONS. 

CHURCHILL SAID THE SOVIET PROPOSALS, BROADCAST BY MOSCOW RADIO, 

HAVE NOT YET BEEN FORMALLY COMMUNICATED TO THE WESTERN POWERS.

CIRCLING ABOVE LONDON AIRPORT IN A RUSSIAN TRANSPORT PLANE. THE PILOT 
OVERSHOT LONDON AIRPORT TWICE BECAUSE HE FAILED TO GRASP QUICKLY 
ENOUGH THE ENGLISH LANGUAGE INSTRUCTIONS RADIOED TO HIM FROM THE AIR- 
PORT CONTROL TOWER.

FT.SILL,. OKLA., FEB. 24 (AP)-A WITNESS AT MAJeAMBRODE He NUGENT'S 
COLLABORATION TRIAL TESTIFIED TODAY THE SENIOR AMERICAN OFFICER IN 
A NORTH KOREAN POW CAMP AUTHORIZED HIM TO MAKE SPEECHES AND BROADCASTS 
DEMANDED BY THEIR COMMUNIST CAPTORS. 

S. SGT. GEORGE MILLWARD, 32, AN AIR FORCE RECRUITER FROM NAMPA, 
IDAHO, SAID LT. COL. PAUL WV. LILES, BIRMINGHAM, ALA., AUTHORIZED 
THE ACTIVITIES. HE SAID LILES STIPULATED THAT PRISONERS SHOULD 
CONSULT HIM FIRST "SO WE WOULDN'T DO ANYTHING DETRIMENTAL TO OUR 
COUNTRY.» 

SGT. MILLWARD WAS THE 15TH DEFENSE WITNESS AS NUGENT'’S GENERAL 
COURT-MARTIAL ON NINE COUNTS OF COLLABORATION WITH THE ENEMY NEARED 
THE END OF THE FIFTH WEEK. IT IS EXPECTED TO WIND UP NEXT WEEK. 

ONE OF THE CHARGES AGAINST NUGENT, 45,.0F MERRILL, WIS., IS THAT 
HE MADE PROPAGANDA SPEECHES AND BROADCASTS DENOUNCING AMERICA’S ENTRY 
IN THE KOREAN WAR. HE IS ALSO ACCUSED OF SIGNING SURRENDER LEAFLETS--

GENEVA, SWITZERLAND, FEB.25 (AP)-THE EUROPEAN ORGANIZATION FOR 
NUCLEAR RESEARCH DECIDED TODAY TO DEFER ACTION ON ANY NEW APPLICATIONS 
FOR MEMBERSHIP IN THE iz-NATION GROUP UNTIL JANUARY, 1957. 

THE ACTION WAS TAKEN AFTER RUMORS CIRCULATED THAT TWO COMMUNIST 
NATIONS OF EASTERN EUROPE WERE SOUNDING OUT THE POSSIBILITY OF 
JOININGs THE COUNCIL OF THE ORGANIZATION SAID NO OFFICIAL 
APPLICATIONS FOR MEMBERSHIP HAVE BEEN RECEIVED. 

THE ORGANIZATION HAS SEVERAL RESEARCH PROJECTS IN PROGRESS AND HAS 
INCREASED ITS STAFF TO i180 MEMBERS. ITS LABORATORIES ON THE 
OUTSKIRTS OF GENEVA ARE STILL UNDER CONSTRUCTIONes IT HOPES TO HAVE A 
SYNCHRO-CYCLOTRON IN OPERATION PRODUCING PROTONS LATE IN 1957. 

ANOTHER MACHINE, A PROTON-SYNCHROTRON, WHICH IS DESIGNED TO 
ACCELERATE PROTONS TO AN EQUIVALENT VOLTAGE OF 25 BILLION VOTS, 

IS EXPECTED TO BE IN OPERATION IN ABOUT 1960.

PHILIPPINE VICE PRESIDENT AND FOREIGN MINISTER CARLOS GARCIA TOLD 
THE CLOSING SESSION THE EIGHT NATIONS "ARE FIRMLY DETERMINED TO SAFE- 
GUARD THEIR PEACE, SECURITY AND FREEDOM AGAINST NOT ONLY AGGRESSION 
BUT SUBVERSION AS WELL THROUGH COLLECTIVE AND CONCERTED ACTION." 

GARCIA SAID THE CONFERENCE "HAS TAKEN A POSITIVE STEP, CALCULATED 
B UNDER EXISTING CIRCUMSTANCES TQ PROMOTE THE ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL WELL 

BEING OF THE PEOPLES OF MEMBER COUNTRIES IN THE TREATY AREA. 

"THE POSITIVE STEPS WE ARE ENVISAGING IN ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL 
FIELDS ATTEST FURTHER TO OUR ABIDING DESIRE TO ENSURE AN ENDURING 
PEACE. 

"DOUBT WAS EXPRESSED IN SEVERAL QUARTERS PREVIOUS TO THIS 
CONFERENCE THAT ANYTHING CONCRETE COULD POSSIBLY BE ACCOMPLISHED 
IN THIS FIRST MEETING OF THE COUNCIL. THE WORK THAT WE HAVE BEEN ABLE 
TO CONCLUDE IN THIS MEETING, WHICH INDEED SURPASSED EXPECTATIONS, 
GIVES US A DEEP SATISFACTION AND PRIDE." 

EDEN SAID THE MEETING HAD GIVEN GOOD THOUGHT “TO THE WORK WE HAVE 
TO DO IF WE ARE TO CONTINUE TO GUIDE AND GUARD THE PEOPLE." 

AND HE PRAISED THAILAND'S HANDLING OF THE CONFERENCE.

A GREAT ORDEAL OF AGGRESSION,” RECOGNIZES THAT THROUGH THE MANILA 
PACT ITS MEMBERS “WILL NOT STAND THE RISK OF HAVING TO STAND ALONE."

ASIAN AND WESTERN NATIONS “WILL SERVE TO SHOW HOW COMPLETELY FALSE" 
COMMUNIST PROPAGANDA IS. 

HE SAID THE MEETING WAS A “REMARKABLE DEMONSTRATION OF WHAT 
CAN BE DONE IN A SHORT TIME" AND WAS "A GOOD AUGURY OF THE FUTURE

LONDON, FEBe 26 (AP)-MOSCOW RADIO CHARGBDYT@DAY THE BANGKOK 
WANILA PACT CONFERENCE WAS AN AMERICAN "CONSP YeeeFOR THE PREPARA- 
ON OF NEW MILITARY ADVENTURES AGAINST THE PEOPLES OF ASIA." 

TWO SOVIET COMMENTATORS BLASTED THE SOUTHEAST ASIA SECURITY CON- 

FERENCE OF EIGHT MANILA PACT NATIONS WHICH ENDED AT BANGKOK YESTERDAY, 

COMMENTATOR We ZAKHAROV SAID THE MEETING OF AN “AGGRESSIVE BLOC oF 
COLONIAL POWERS AND THEIR PUPPETS" PRIMARILY WAS AIMED AT WRECKING 
THE GENEVA AGREEMENTS. 

THE GENEVA AGREEMENTS, HE SAID, “FORBID VIET NAM, LAOS AND 
CAMBODIA TO TAKE PART IN ANY MILITARY GROUPINGS. THE TALKS IN BANGKOK 
PROVIDED FOR THE INTEGRATION OF THE SOUTHERN PART OF VIET NAM, LAOS 
AND CAMBODIA INTO THE AGGRESSIVE MANILA PACT." 

ZAKHAROV CLAIMED THE CONFERENCE ®TOOK PLACE IN AN ATMOSPHERE OF 
ACUTE DIFFERENCESe" BETWEEN BRITAIN, FRANCE AND THE UNITED STATES, 

COMMENTATOR MIKHAIL SLAVYANOV SAID "IT WAS NOT PEACE AND FREEDOW 
THAT THEY WERE DISCUSSING BEHIND CLOSED DOORS IN BANGKOK BUT HOW 
TO THROTTLE AHD ASIAN PEOPLES DESIRE FOR FREEDOM AND PEACE, HOW TO 
MAINTAIN TENSION IN THE FAR EAST." 

HE TERMED SECRETARY OF STATE DULLES A "NEW KIND OF ROVING DIPLOMA 
PROPAGANDIST.® 

"TODAY THEY MAKE FLORID ORATIONS SOMEWHERE ON THE TERRITORY OF THE 
UeSeAs AND TOMORROW YOU CAN HEAR THEM IN BANGKOK," SLAVYANOV SAID. 
*THESE ROAMING DIPLOMATS MAKE SPEECHES, GIVE INTERVIEWS AND HURL 
INSULTS AT THEIR OPPONENTS, NOT FORGETTING IN THE MEANWHILE TO AVOW 
THEIR LOVE FOR PEACE AND TO GIVE INSTRUCTIONS TO PEOPLE WITHOUT END."

(400) BAYONET FIGHTING . 

BY CeYATES MCDANIEL aX; 
(ADVANCE) WASHINGTON, FEB. 26 (AP) -THB?U.Se MARINES 
COLD STEEL WILL BE IMPORTANT EVEN IN ATOMIC WAR, ARE TESTING OUT A 
NEW SYSTEM OF BAYONET FIGHTING. 

THE FIRST IMPROVEMENT IN SUCH COMBAT IN 50 YEARS, IT IS BASED 

THE ART OF BOXING, AND STRESSES AGGRESSIVENESS. 

WORKED OUT BY A FORMER ARMY SOLDIER, THE SYSTEM HAS BEEN TESTED 
AT QUANTICO, VAs, AND PARRIS ISLAND, SeCe, AND AWAITS ONLY THE FINAL 
APPROVAL OF THE COMMANDANT BEFORE BECOMING STANDARD TRAINING. 

THE MARINES AND THE ARMY HAVE BEEN USING A BAYONET SYSTEM DEVISED 
AT THE BEGINNING OF THIS CENTURY. BOTH SERVICES REEMPHASIZED AND 
MODERNIZED THEIR BAYONET TECHNIQUES AFTER STUDYING THE RUSSO-JAPANESE 
WAR IN 1904-1905. THAT BAYONET SYSTEM WAS CARRIED INTO WORLD WAR I 
WITH SOME MODIFICATIONS BORROWED FROM THE BRITISH ARMY.~ 

BUT MARINE OFFICERS SAY NOW THAT THE HISTORIC CONCEPT OF THE USE 
OF THE BAYONET IS STILL TOO TRADITIONALLY TIED TO THE MEDIEVAL USE 
OF THE PIKE, A SHARP METAL SPIKE MOUNTED ON A LONG WOODEN HANDLE. 

THE NEW SYSTEM DEVELOPED BY ARMOND He SEIDLER, AN ARMY VETERAN OF 
WORLD WAR I1 WHO WROTE HIS DOCTOR'S THESIS ON THE ART OF HAND-TO-HAND 
COMBAT, DISCARDS THE ANCIENT CONCEPTS AND FOLLOWS MORE CLOSELY THE 
SCIENCE OF MODERN BOXING. | 

"IF YOU CAN THROW A LEFT HOOK, A ROUNDHOUSE RIGHT OR AN UPPERCUT," 
AN OFFICIAL MARINE CORPS STATEMENT SAID, “YOU CAN LEARN THIS NEW 
SYSTEM OF BAYONET FIGHTING IN A MATTER OF MINUTES." 

ONE MARINE OFFICER SAID THE SAME THING-A LITTLE MORE BLUNTLY? 

"WHAT WE ARE TRYPNG TO DO IS TO LET MARINES USE THEIR NATURAL FIGHTING 
INSTINCTS, THE ROUGHER THE BETTER.” 

THE BAYONET WAS INVENTED IN THE TOWN OF BAYONNE IN SOUTHERN FRANCE 
IN THE 15TH CENTURY. BECAUSE ARMIES OF THAT TIME COULD NOT FIGURE 
OUT A PRACTICAL WAY TO ATTACH IT TO OTHZR WEAPONS IT WAS SLOW TO WIN 
APPROVAL. 

BRITISH SOLDIERS OF THAT OLD TIME COMPLAINED THAT IT WAS GOOD 
FNOUGHT FOR ANY SOUTHERN EUROPEANS WHO WANTED TO GO ABOUT SLASHING 
THEMSELVES BUT LOYAL ENGLISHMEN MUCH PREFERRED TO CLUB EACH OTHER TO 
DEATH IF THEY HAD TO. 

BUT AFTER AN ENGLISH ARMY FORCE LOST A BATTLE OR TWO BECAUSE THEY 
FAILED TO USE THEIR BAYONETY PROPERLY, THE WEAPON WAS MODERNIZED AND 
MADE A STANDARD PIECE OF EQUIPMENT. 

BAYONET FIGHTING PLAYED ONLY A SMALL PART IN WORLD WAR II. BUT IN 
THE FIXED POSITION WARFARE OF THE LATTER PHASES OF THE CONFLICT IN 
KOREA IT STAGED SOMETHING OF A COMEBACK THAT THE MARINES HAVE NOT 
FORGOTTEN.
